# Repository Guidelines

## Linear Issue-First Workflow

Linear is the shared source of truth for planned and active Evorto work. Use the
`evorto` team (`EVO`) in <https://linear.app/evorto> so collaborators can see plans,
avoid duplicate work, and add missing context before implementation.

- Before implementation or repository edits, search existing Linear issues and
  related branches/PRs. Reuse the canonical issue when the work overlaps; do not
  create a second competing plan or silently take over someone else's work.
- Create or update the issue **before starting work**, including work requested
  in chat. Record the goal, scope, proposed approach, acceptance criteria,
  dependencies, and verification plan. Keep this proportional to the change.
- Make ownership and status visible before implementation. Identify the person
  or agent doing the work, coordinate overlapping efforts, and link related
  issues. Split independent work into linked issues with clear boundaries.
- Call out missing product/history context and open decisions explicitly so
  Lukas can add what he knows. Ask a specific question and wait when its answer
  could materially change scope or behavior; do not turn an assumption into a
  decision. Routine work with sufficient context need not wait for approval.
- Keep the issue current as the plan changes. Record blockers, decisions,
  meaningful progress, and handoffs there instead of leaving them only in chat
  or a local plan. Put newly discovered follow-up work in issues before starting
  it, and distinguish required scope from optional follow-ups.
- Include the `EVO-<number>` identifier in commits and PRs, and link the resulting
  PR or direct commit back to the issue. Close it only after recording what
  shipped, the verification performed, and any remaining follow-ups.
- If Linear is unavailable, report the blocker and prepare a draft plan without
  starting implementation. Do not silently bypass issue-first coordination.

This workflow does not replace the verification, branching, release-note, or
publication requirements below. Direct-to-main permission for one change is not
standing permission for later changes.

## Context Discipline

- Keep repository knowledge in small, relevant files.
- Use this file as the map, not the full manual.
- Read the nearest applicable guidance before editing:
  - root product/system context
  - module-level `AGENTS.md`
  - local README files
- Update context files when reality changes, assumptions are invalidated, or new constraints are discovered.
- Prefer small, accurate updates over large stale manuals.

## Root Context Files

- `PRODUCT.md` - product goals, personas, core workflows, domain concepts, and product invariants.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` - high-level system shape, architectural boundaries, and where to look first for common changes.
- `QUALITY.md` - behavior-focused verification guidance, Browser/Playwright expectations, and done criteria.

Keep these files concise. Put implementation-specific guidance in the nearest module-level `AGENTS.md` or README.

## Project Structure

- App code: `src/app/**`
- Server runtime and APIs: `src/server/**`
- Data layer: `src/db/**`
- Shared contracts/types/utilities: `src/shared/**` and `src/types/**`
- Unit tests: `*.spec.ts` in `src/**`
- Playwright tests: `tests/**`
- Legacy e2e reference: `e2e/**`
- Assets/public: `public/`
- Theming: `src/styles.scss` and `_theme-colors.scss`

Start with the nearest applicable module guidance:

- `src/app/AGENTS.md`
- `src/server/AGENTS.md`
- `src/db/AGENTS.md`
- `tests/AGENTS.md`

More specific guidance may exist deeper in some subtrees.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `bun run dev:start` - resolve local settings in memory and run the Angular dev server on the resolved `APP_HOST_PORT`.
- `bun run build:app` - build client + server bundles.
- `bun run test:unit` - run unit tests.
- `bun run test:unit:server` - run server unit tests.
- `bun run test:integration:postgres` - run the fail-closed PostgreSQL 17 integration suite.
- `bun run test:integration:postgres:local` - run that suite with supported local dotenv configuration.
- `bun run test:e2e` - run Playwright e2e.
- `bun run test:e2e:baseline` - run complete functional and documentation baselines with shared setup and guide export.
- `bun run test:e2e:docs` - run Playwright documentation tests.
- `bun run test:e2e:integration` - run credential-gated integration Playwright projects.
- `bun run test:e2e:live-esncard:release` - run the full live-provider release certification locally.
- `bun run test:e2e:install` - install the local Playwright browser binaries.
- `bun run lint` - lint with autofix.
- `bun run format:check` - verify formatting without changing files.
- `bun run format:write` - format with Prettier.
- `bun run docker:start` / `bun run docker:stop` - start/stop local services;
  `docker:start` may reset local data and should leave enough seeded data to
  get going from zero.
- `bun run docker:resume` - bring back the existing `db`, `minio`, `stripe`,
  and `evorto` containers without recreating them or rerunning the one-shot
  setup services; it refuses incomplete or unsuccessfully initialized stacks.
- `bun run db:push`, `bun run db:reset` - database commands.

## Local Environment

Codex environment setup refreshes a clean worktree to the parent/source branch
tip before installing dependencies and generating `.env.dev`. If local changes
already exist, setup skips branch refresh rather than overwriting work.
For a new linked worktree, setup also copies a missing `.env` from the primary
checkout with owner-only permissions. An existing worktree `.env` is preserved.

Supported local env files:

- `.env` - untracked developer secrets
- `.env.dev.local` - tracked shared dev config
- `.env.dev` - generated worktree override from `bun run env:runtime`

Unsupported files:

- `.env.local`
- `.env.runtime`
- `.env.ci`

In CI, do not rely on tracked or generated dotenv artifacts. Use GitHub Actions `env`, `vars`, and `secrets`.

For runtime/test details, read:

- `tests/README.md`
- `helpers/README.md`
- `src/server/config/AGENTS.md`

Local `test:e2e`, `test:e2e:baseline`, `test:e2e:ui`, `test:e2e:docs`, `db:*`, and `docker:*`
package scripts use `env:run` to resolve an invocation-private environment in memory.
They never read the shared `.env.dev` snapshot. Use these scripts or
`bun run env:run -- <command>` instead of chaining `env:runtime` and `dotenv`.
`env:runtime` remains an atomic, owner-only `.env.dev` snapshot writer for
standalone inspection. Child commands preserve process environment values over
`.env.dev.local`, generated runtime defaults, and `.env`, in that order.

## Type Safety

- End-to-end types are mandatory.
- Prefer inferred/derived types from Drizzle schema and Effect schema outputs.
- Prefer TypeScript return type inference unless explicit return types clarify a boundary or prevent incorrect inference from escaping.
- Avoid `any`, unchecked `as`, and `unknown` without narrowing.
- Do not use `unknown as ...` or similar cast bypasses to force client/server types to compile.
- Fix the source type contract or runtime mismatch instead.

## Error Handling

- Do not swallow defects.
- If an error is expected and recoverable, map it explicitly to a typed/domain outcome.
- If an error is unexpected, fail loudly and preserve enough context to debug it.
- RPC and Effect error channels use `Schema.TaggedError` end to end.
- Do not introduce string-literal business errors in contracts or handlers.
- Only expected recoverable failures belong in typed error unions.
- When an external unknown error must cross a typed boundary, wrap it in a tagged error field using `Schema.Defect`.

## Architecture Guardrails

- Angular app guidance lives in `src/app/AGENTS.md`.
- Server/runtime guidance lives in `src/server/AGENTS.md`.
- Database guidance lives in `src/db/AGENTS.md`.
- Use Angular Material components and Tailwind styling with the existing semantic theme tokens.
- For UI design, refinement, and review, read `.agents/skills/design-taste-frontend/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/project-design/SKILL.md`. Taste replaces the former `uncodixfy` and `material-3` skills; project requirements govern stack, tokens, accessibility, and behavior.
- Use Effect RPC and Effect Schema for API boundaries.
- Use Drizzle as the source of truth for persisted shapes.
- Use Stripe as the source of truth for payment state.
- Keep tenant isolation, auth, payments, registration, and permissions explicit.

## Deployment and Schema

- Scaleway deployments explain and apply the Drizzle schema through the private
  `ops` role before releasing the worker and web roles at the same digest.
- Review schema changes for compatibility with the currently deployed app. Use
  expand/contract steps for destructive or otherwise backward-incompatible
  changes unless the release is explicitly coordinated as a maintenance window.

## Vendored Repositories

- External source repositories are vendored under `repos/` as read-only reference material.
- When writing Effect code, read `repos/effect/LLMS.md` first, then inspect `repos/effect/packages/**` for Effect v4 implementation details, tests, module structure, and idiomatic patterns.
- When changing Drizzle schema, queries, migrations, or relational query behavior, inspect `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/src/**`, `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/tests/**`, and `repos/drizzle/integration-tests/**` for current upstream behavior and examples.
- Prefer vendored upstream sources over web search or generated guesses when library behavior or composition is unclear.
- Do not edit files under `repos/` unless explicitly asked.
- Do not import from `repos/`; application code must continue importing from normal package dependencies such as `effect`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/sql-pg`, and `drizzle-orm`.

## Verification

- Before any push, PR update, or other action that can trigger CI, run the full
  local equivalent of every CI test suite that the change will trigger. Every
  collected test must pass: zero failures, skips, todos, fixmes, expected
  failures, retries/flakes, interrupted tests, or focused tests. Missing local
  services, environment variables, or credentials are blockers to resolve, not
  reasons to defer coverage to CI. CI confirms an already-green local result;
  it is never the first full test run.
- After every file edit, run `bun run lint` and `bun run format:write`.
- Lint covers application, test, helper, and root TypeScript config sources
  while excluding vendored `repos/`. Node-side helper/config tooling uses the
  shared TypeScript correctness rules without Angular UI or deterministic
  sort-order rules.
- Markdown-only edits do not need a WebStorm `get_file_problems` pass.
- Before calling WebStorm `get_file_problems` on edited files, run `bun run lint`.
- After editing non-Markdown files, run WebStorm `get_file_problems` on those files when possible.
- Prefer sequential `get_file_problems` checks; parallel runs can time out.
- For UI behavior changes, use Browser verification where useful and add/update Playwright coverage for durable behavior.
- For generated documentation flows, keep Playwright docs current.
- See `QUALITY.md` for done criteria and Browser/Playwright guidance.

## Conventions

- TypeScript strict mode is enforced.
- Indentation: 2 spaces.
- Filenames: `kebab-case.ts`.
- Symbols: `camelCase` and `PascalCase`.
- Prefer path aliases: `@app/*`, `@server/*`, `@db/*`, `@shared/*`, `@helpers/*`.
- Import `src/types/**` directly; TypeScript reserves the `@types/*` package
  namespace and rejects that path form in production builds.
- For Effect reference and usage patterns, consult the local Effect source at `/Users/hedde/code/effect` when behavior or recommended composition is unclear.

## Commit, PR, and Release Notes

- Use Git Town commands for branch management and shipping.
- For substantial work in a new worktree created from `main`, immediately run `git town hack <branch-name>` before making commits.
- For large multi-phase work, keep an assembly branch plus one reviewable child branch per phase or slice.
- Create stacked child branches with `git town append <branch-name>`.
- Run `git town sync --stack` before starting work and before proposing review.
- Open PRs with `git town propose`.
- Commit messages should be imperative and concise.
- PRs should include purpose, scope, schema/runtime impact, and UI evidence where relevant.
- Every PR needs a new Knope change file in `.changeset/*.md`, including
  test-only and CI-only changes. The hosted Knope Bot enforces this requirement.
- Before starting full verification, check that the PR diff includes its change
  file. `knope --validate` checks configuration and file validity; it does not
  check whether the current PR adds a change file.
# Shared Astra backlog

The user keeps a machine-wide backlog of valuable work for spare Astra usage, reviewed Fridays at 12:00 Europe/Berlin.

- Canonical backlog: `/Users/hedde/Documents/Codex/2026-11-04/my/outputs/astra-backlog.md`.
- When project work reveals a non-urgent task that would benefit materially from Astra-level reasoning, add a concise, actionable entry there. Read first, deduplicate, preserve other entries, and re-read before saving concurrent edits.
- Record project/path, source chat or PR, problem and evidence, why Astra would help, priority, completion criteria, and status. Label speculative ideas as candidates until verified.
- Do not defer urgent or already-requested work just to save it for Friday. Keep routine work with the appropriate model.
- The user interacts with the main chat; it owns task selection, coordination, integration, and reporting. Recording a task or receiving the reminder does not authorize automatic execution, release actions, or a model switch.
- Friday review should select the highest-value ready items based on available usage. Verify remaining usage and the next reset when available; do not assume the reset is weekly or always Friday. Never invent account usage figures.

# Hand-Off Session

## Response Format

Begin the first response to this skill invocation with the line:

`Entire Session Handoff:`

followed by a blank line, then the content. Apply the header to the **first response of the invocation only** — not on follow-up turns and not on error / early-exit responses (no sessions found, transcript missing). Its presence signals the skill ran and produced real output. The "Unanswered Question" branch still gets the header.

## STOP — Read these rules before doing ANYTHING

1. **Do NOT ask clarifying questions.** Auto-detect the session and read the transcript.
2. **Do NOT run** `git log`, `git status`, `git branch`, `ps aux`, or any other exploratory commands. Use only the `entire` CLI commands listed below.
3. **Do NOT say** "Would you like me to continue?" or "Let me know if you want me to pick this up." Just read the transcript and start working. Exception: if the previous agent asked the user a question that was never answered, you MUST ask the user that question before proceeding.

Required CLI: entire 0.6.2+ (`session list --json`, `session info --transcript`, `session current --json|--transcript`, `checkpoint explain --json|--transcript|--raw-transcript --session-index N`). If a flag is rejected, tell the user to upgrade and stop.

## Flow: Active session handoff (default — also covers bare invocation and "current"/"active")

### Step 1: Resolve the canonical worktree path

```bash
entire session current --json
```

If the output is valid JSON, read its `worktree_path` field — that is **the** canonical worktree root for this invocation, set by Entire itself. Use it verbatim in the next step (no `cwd` heuristic needed; symlinks, `/private/var`/`/var` quirks, and subdirectory invocation are all handled).

If the output is not JSON (Entire prints `No active session found in this worktree.` when nothing is active), set the canonical worktree path to `null` and rely on the bidirectional prefix-match fallback in Step 2.

### Step 2: Pick the session

```bash
entire session list --json
```

Each entry has `session_id`, `agent`, `status`, `worktree_path`, `started_at`, `last_active`, `turns`, `last_prompt`, `files_touched`. Apply filters in this order:

1. **Worktree scope.** If you got a canonical worktree path in Step 1, keep entries where `worktree_path` equals it exactly. Otherwise, keep entries where `cwd` starts with `worktree_path` **or** `worktree_path` starts with `cwd`. If either filter yields zero entries, fall back to the unscoped list — better to summarize a slightly-off session than to refuse the handoff.
2. **User-named agent filter** (optional). If the user said "codex", "claude", "kiro", "gemini", etc., keep only entries whose `agent` matches case-insensitively as a substring (so `gemini` matches `Gemini CLI`).
3. **Drop self.** Drop entries where `agent` matches the agent currently running this skill (e.g. `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Cursor`, `Gemini CLI`, `Copilot CLI`, `Factory AI Droid`, `OpenCode`). **If this empties the list**, undo this filter and keep self — the user is asking you to summarize *your own* current session for compaction. Note that fact in the announcement (Step 5).
4. **Pick most recent.** Sort by `last_active` (fall back to `started_at`) descending; take the first.

If filtering still leaves zero entries (truly nothing in the list, even self), print a one-line error (no header) and stop.

### Step 3: Stream the raw transcript

```bash
entire session info <session_id> --transcript > /tmp/handoff-<session_id>.jsonl
```

Snapshot is bounded to the file size at command start. Output is JSONL for most agents and a single JSON document for Gemini CLI.

### Step 4: Extract conversation content

**JSONL agents** (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Copilot CLI / Factory AI Droid / OpenCode):

```bash
grep -E '"type":"(message|function_call|user|assistant)"' /tmp/handoff-<session_id>.jsonl | cut -c1-2000 | head -20    # original task
grep -E '"type":"(message|function_call|user|assistant)"' /tmp/handoff-<session_id>.jsonl | cut -c1-2000 | tail -100   # final state
```

**Gemini CLI** (single JSON document — no JSONL grep):

```bash
jq 'keys' /tmp/handoff-<session_id>.jsonl
```

The top-level shape varies by Gemini CLI version, but messages live under one of `messages`, `contents`, `history`, or `turns`. Each entry has a `role` (`user`/`model`/`function`/`tool`) and a content payload under one of `parts[].text`, `content`, or `text`. Extract role + text in chronological order:

```bash
# Example — adapt the path based on what `jq 'keys'` showed.
jq -r '.messages[] | "\(.role): \([.parts[]? | .text // ""] | join(" "))"' /tmp/handoff-<session_id>.jsonl | head -20
jq -r '.messages[] | "\(.role): \([.parts[]? | .text // ""] | join(" "))"' /tmp/handoff-<session_id>.jsonl | tail -100
```

If neither shape works, fall back to the Read tool on the JSON file and locate the message array by inspection.

Do not show the raw extracted lines to the user. They are inputs for Step 5.

### Step 5: Announce, summarize, present

**Announcement.** First line of the body: `Handing off <agent> session — <turns> turns, last active <relative time>, ID <first-8-of-session-id>.` If the picked session is your own (Step 2 self-filter fallback), prepend a one-clause note: `Self-handoff (no other sessions in this worktree)`. This gives the user a chance to catch a wrong pick before reading the summary.

**Summary structure** (skip any section with no genuine content — do **not** hallucinate filler):

1. **Task Overview** — the user's core request, success criteria, stated constraints.
2. **Current State** — completed work: files created/modified, key decisions, artifacts produced.
3. **Important Discoveries** — technical constraints found, rationale behind decisions, errors hit and how they were resolved, failed approaches and why.
4. **Next Steps** — specific remaining actions, blockers, priority ordering.
5. **Context to Preserve** — user preferences, domain details, commitments made during the session.

# Linear

## Overview

This skill provides a structured workflow for managing issues, projects & team workflows in Linear. It ensures consistent integration with the Linear MCP server, which offers natural-language project management for issues, projects, documentation, and team collaboration.

## Prerequisites
- Linear MCP server must be connected and accessible via OAuth
- Confirm access to the relevant Linear workspace, teams, and projects

## Required Workflow

**Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.**

### Step 0: Set up Linear MCP (if not already configured)

If any MCP call fails because Linear MCP is not connected, pause and set it up:

1. Add the Linear MCP:
   - `codex mcp add linear --url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`
2. Enable remote MCP client:
   - Set `[features] rmcp_client = true` in `config.toml` **or** run `codex --enable rmcp_client`
3. Log in with OAuth:
   - `codex mcp login linear`

After successful login, the user will have to restart codex. You should finish your answer and tell them so when they try again they can continue with Step 1.

**Windows/WSL note:** If you see connection errors on Windows, try configuring the Linear MCP to run via WSL:
```json
{"mcpServers": {"linear": {"command": "wsl", "args": ["npx", "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.linear.app/sse", "--transport", "sse-only"]}}}
```

### Step 1
Clarify the user's goal and scope (e.g., issue triage, sprint planning, documentation audit, workload balance). Confirm team/project, priority, labels, cycle, and due dates as needed.

### Step 2
Select the appropriate workflow (see Practical Workflows below) and identify the Linear MCP tools you will need. Confirm required identifiers (issue ID, project ID, team key) before calling tools.

### Step 3
Execute Linear MCP tool calls in logical batches:
- Read first (list/get/search) to build context.
- Create or update next (issues, projects, labels, comments) with all required fields.
- For bulk operations, explain the grouping logic before applying changes.

### Step 4
Summarize results, call out remaining gaps or blockers, and propose next actions (additional issues, label changes, assignments, or follow-up comments).

## Available Tools

Issue Management: `list_issues`, `get_issue`, `create_issue`, `update_issue`, `list_my_issues`, `list_issue_statuses`, `list_issue_labels`, `create_issue_label`

Project & Team: `list_projects`, `get_project`, `create_project`, `update_project`, `list_teams`, `get_team`, `list_users`

Documentation & Collaboration: `list_documents`, `get_document`, `search_documentation`, `list_comments`, `create_comment`, `list_cycles`

## Practical Workflows

- Sprint Planning: Review open issues for a target team, pick top items by priority, and create a new cycle (e.g., "Q1 Performance Sprint") with assignments.
- Bug Triage: List critical/high-priority bugs, rank by user impact, and move the top items to "In Progress."
- Documentation Audit: Search documentation (e.g., API auth), then open labeled "documentation" issues for gaps or outdated sections with detailed fixes.
- Team Workload Balance: Group active issues by assignee, flag anyone with high load, and suggest or apply redistributions.
- Release Planning: Create a project (e.g., "v2.0 Release") with milestones (feature freeze, beta, docs, launch) and generate issues with estimates.
- Cross-Project Dependencies: Find all "blocked" issues, identify blockers, and create linked issues if missing.
- Automated Status Updates: Find your issues with stale updates and add status comments based on current state/blockers.
- Smart Labeling: Analyze unlabeled issues, suggest/apply labels, and create missing label categories.
- Sprint Retrospectives: Generate a report for the last completed cycle, note completed vs. pushed work, and open discussion issues for patterns.

## Tips for Maximum Productivity

- Batch operations for related changes; consider smart templates for recurring issue structures.
- Use natural queries when possible ("Show me what John is working on this week").
- Leverage context: reference prior issues in new requests.
- Break large updates into smaller batches to avoid rate limits; cache or reuse filters when listing frequently.

## Troubleshooting

- Authentication: Clear browser cookies, re-run OAuth, verify workspace permissions, ensure API access is enabled.
- Tool Calling Errors: Confirm the model supports multiple tool calls, provide all required fields, and split complex requests.
- Missing Data: Refresh token, verify workspace access, check for archived projects, and confirm correct team selection.
- Performance: Remember Linear API rate limits; batch bulk operations, use specific filters, or cache frequent queries.

issues.body:
## Purpose

Simplify Evorto's root tooling around Codex and Claude, matching the clarified EVO-8 scope. The earlier module-guidance rewrite is reverted from this PR.

Linear: https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude

## Changes

- Remove the tracked Air, Gemini, Entire, JetBrains and VS Code config folders.
- Remove Entire session-recording lifecycle hooks, its Codex hook feature toggle, and the Copilot cloud-agent setup. Retain required Copilot code review and its source-only setup.
- Keep Codex MCP/worktree setup and shared skills, EditorConfig, Prettier and ESLint configuration. Add a small CLAUDE.md that imports the canonical AGENTS.md.
- Remove git-town.toml and the Git Town stack-display workflow. Replace mandatory Git Town commands with ordinary Git/GitHub PR guidance and optional GitHub-native stacked PRs.
- Ignore retired tool/editor directories so local settings do not return to source control. Add a Knope change file.

## Project-local cleanup

Entire's session-recording Git hooks and agent hooks/settings were removed from all seven existing Evorto worktrees. Hook/session metadata was archived recoverably outside the repository. Global tools/settings, other projects, historical commits/branch refs, and inactive historical Git Town branch metadata were preserved. Those local uninstall steps are not represented by the tracked diff; existing checkouts outside this machine should disable their own installed Entire hooks when adopting the change.

GitHub confirms native stacked PRs are generally available on all github.com plans: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-06-stacked-pull-requests-generally-available/ . The optional gh stack extension provides local stack automation; ordinary Git remains usable. No extension installation or protection-rule change is included here.

## Compatibility with the planned hosting move

The removal concerns optional session recording/checkpoints, not Entire Git hosting. Entire's documented repository workflow uses CLI/git-remote-entire, authentication and a native remote; `entire enable` adds session capture separately. Installed CLI/global settings are untouched. The planned hosting/RWX migration is tracked in [EVO-50](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test); it will create a new repository from one approved main snapshot with a new initial commit, while preserving existing history separately. This PR does not perform that migration, re-enable capture, switch remotes, or cancel GitHub. Current PR/Linear/Copilot and verification requirements remain in force until an authorized cutover.

Official references: [Entire repository guide](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository), [CLI recording setup](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md), [RWX integration](https://www.rwx.com/docs/getting-started/entire).

## Verification

Re-run for clarified head `6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd`.

- Frozen dependency installation, Knope, formatting, lint and diff checks passed. Lint reports three pre-existing warnings.
- Server unit tests: 2,692 passed. Application unit tests: 1,707 passed. PostgreSQL integration tests: 383 passed.
- Terraform validation and HIGH/CRITICAL config scan passed.
- Linux/amd64 image build, runtime/size/source-map checks, SBOM and HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability scan passed.
- Functional/documentation baseline: all 275 tests passed in 3.3 minutes; the isolated stack was removed and original local app restoration verified.
- Retained entrypoint/ignore checks and project-wide Entire-hook removal assertions passed. Independent read-only review found no actionable regression.

No application behavior, schema, deployment or UI changes. No direct-main push or merge. Copilot completed a fresh review of this exact head and recommended approval with no open issues.


## Review and hosted validation

- [Copilot review of 6de30fa7a39](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/209#pullrequestreview-5817220698): approval recommended, no actionable comments or unresolved threads. Copilot skipped the 18 deleted generated .idea files; those deletions and retained shared settings were checked locally.
- [PR Quality](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/actions/runs/42463471253): all required jobs and CI/gate passed on the same head. CodeQL and source-only Copilot setup also passed. Optional CodeRabbit skipped this draft.
- PR remains a draft and unmerged.

issues.body:
A Stripe webhook handler that runs longer than five minutes can lose its claim to a retry. Previously, its late failure deleted the retry's receipt, and its late success could mark that receipt processed while the retry was still running.

Give every receipt attempt a fresh PostgreSQL-generated UUID, including stale-claim takeovers. Completion and release now require the exact event, attempt token, and processing status. Keep payment transitions and their existing transactional guards unchanged.

Validation:

- Added three real PostgreSQL regressions for late failure, late success, and immediate release/replacement at an identical timestamp. All three fail with the former event-only mutation predicates and pass with the fix.
- Complete local browser/documentation baseline: 275 passed, zero skipped/retried.
- Complete local server suite: 2,692 passed.
- Complete local Angular suite: 1,707 passed.
- Complete local PostgreSQL suite: 386 passed, zero skipped.
- Lint passes with three existing warnings; formatting and Knope validation pass.
- Local infrastructure validation/security scan and Linux/amd64 runtime build, inspection, SBOM, and HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability scan pass.

Schema/runtime review: Evorto is not deployed, so no live-upgrade compatibility path is required. Adds non-null `stripe_webhook_events.claim_id` with a database UUID default. Verified the additive upgrade against synthetic pre-change processing and processed receipts: all existing fields and microsecond timestamps were preserved exactly, each existing row received a distinct token, and new receipts received their own default token. Real local data was untouched. Fencing protects receipt ownership, while business-side idempotency remains the responsibility of the existing payment transactions. Local tests use synthetic data, a separate disposable PostgreSQL 17 container, and Stripe mocks/test mode. No production data, credential changes, merge, or deployment.

Review the token renewal on takeover, both conditional terminal writes, and propagation of the owned token through the handler's normal and failure paths.

- `main` <!-- branch-stack -->
  - **fix: preserve recovered Stripe webhook claim ownership** :point\_left:

{"id":"EVO-50","uuid":"290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e","title":"Move Evorto to Entire and RWX with smaller workflows and reliable test selection","description":"## Outcome

Host evorto-app/app natively on Entire and rebuild CI/CD on RWX. Replace oversized, repeated workflow setup with small tasks and an understandable test-selection interface shared by local agents and CI. Cancel the paid GitHub subscription after the replacement is proven.

The user selected RWX and is comfortable rebuilding jobs rather than preserving GitHub Actions YAML. Budget is small; determine actual GitHub savings and measure RWX usage rather than assuming either amount.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Scope

* Inventory current checks, integrations, protections, release automation, credentials and costs.
* Define named verification suites and conservative, explainable change-based selection.
* Rebuild quality, integration, browser and image verification as focused RWX tasks.
* Migrate Git hosting, review and required checks to Entire.
* Rebuild staging, release certification and production promotion.
* Validate coverage, reliability, cost and rollback before cutover and subscription cancellation.

## Existing evidence and coordination

Current workflows include Bun/Angular unit tests, PostgreSQL integration, Docker Compose with Playwright, Terraform checks, image/runtime verification, SBOM/vulnerability scans, provider certification and Scaleway deployment. GitHub-specific dependencies include environments, workflow chaining, gh API/release calls, Knope and PR tooling; audit current main and active branches before implementation.

<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> currently removes Entire hooks and Git Town requirements; <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> establishes PR-only publication and Linear-linked naming. Reconcile these with the new hosting direction without blindly reverting cleanup or losing protected review. Keep Linear tracking for this migration; migrating the wider issue backlog to Trails is a separate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

* Entire is the canonical Git remote, initialized from the agreed main snapshot as one new initial commit with no imported ancestry. Verify the snapshot against its recorded source SHA, preserve the old repository recoverably, and verify access, review and required-check protections.
* RWX runs the required suites and reports usable checks to Trails.
* Local and hosted verification use the same documented suite definitions and selection rules.
* Selection explains its decisions, supports a full run, and falls back to broad coverage for unknown/shared/high-risk changes. No skipped tests or reduced coverage are disguised as a complete run.
* Repeated setup and builds are shared where safe; deployment and live-provider checks execute fresh.
* Staging and production use the same verified image digest, with schema compatibility, serialization and explicit production approval preserved.
* A complete change-to-production trial, rollback procedure and measured cost are recorded before cutover.
* Cancel the verified GitHub subscription only after replacement readiness; preserve recoverable repository/archive data and check effects on other repositories.

## Execution

Complete the linked subissues in dependency order. This issue records the plan; creating it does not execute migrations, deployments or subscription changes.

References: [repository](<https://github.com/evorto-app/app>), [Entire + RWX](<https://entire.com/blog/ci-with-rwx-is-now-available-on-entire>), [RWX pricing](<https://www.rwx.com/pricing>), [RWX caching](<https://www.rwx.com/docs/caching>).","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test","gitBranchName":"evo-50-move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows","createdAt":"2026-11-08T08:08:22.785Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-08T08:25:46.722Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"c813509e-14a4-492a-8321-befcd8b38d7e","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-11-08T08:08:22.785Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Lukas Heddendorp","createdById":"5de66975-4b30-495f-a21e-303534976d2d","team":"evorto","teamId":"f7bdbd43-80e0-420d-b538-f1d2be041725","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"EVO-8","title":"Simplify root tooling for Codex and Claude"},{"id":"EVO-9","title":"Require PRs and document Linear-linked naming"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

Updated draft PR209: <pull-request id="f40ef9c3-4325-4743-93cf-c25b6f4da34d" label="evorto-app/app#209" href="https://linear.app/evorto/review/evo-8-simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude-b853eb8ba03a" /> . All local gates and required remote CI passed; fresh Copilot review recommends approval with no open issues. The PR remains draft, open and unmerged. Await Lukas's review/merge decision.

## Scope delivered

* Remove five root tool/editor config folders: .air, .gemini, .entire, .idea and .vscode. Remove optional Entire recording hooks and Copilot cloud-agent setup.
* Keep Codex MCP/features/worktree setup, shared skills, EditorConfig, Prettier and ESLint. Add CLAUDE.md importing the canonical AGENTS.md.
* Keep source-only Copilot review setup and the review requirement. Remove git-town.toml and the stack-display workflow; replace mandatory Git Town commands with normal Git/GitHub and optional native stacks.
* Revert the earlier unrelated module/skill/layout rewrite. Add a Knope change file and ignore local retired-tool state. Final diff: 36 files, +61/-559 lines, with no application/runtime/schema changes.
* Archive active Entire recording hooks/session metadata recoverably outside the repository across seven existing Evorto worktrees. Preserve global settings and installed tools, other projects, historical refs and inactive Git Town branch metadata.

## Hosting-plan compatibility

The <issue id="290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e" label="EVO-50" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test" />/<issue id="66c4077f-4104-439f-97bf-5a57f6a7dc79" label="EVO-54" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-54/migrate-git-hosting-and-protected-review-to-entire" /> migration is separate planning, not executed by this PR. Entire Git hosting uses CLI/git-remote-entire, authentication and a native remote; `entire enable` adds optional recording. RWX uses its Entire integration and workflow definitions, not the removed agent hooks. Existing CLI 0.13.1 and git-remote-entire remain untouched. The GitHub origin and current PR/Linear/Copilot protections remain until authorized cutover.

The future repository should start from one approved main snapshot and a new initial commit; preserve old history and pending work separately. Do not import checkpoint refs or restore stale recording hooks merely for hosting. No migration, history rewrite or GitHub cancellation occurred.

References: [https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository](<https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository>) ; [https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md](<https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md>) ; [https://www.rwx.com/docs/getting-started/entire](<https://www.rwx.com/docs/getting-started/entire>) . Codex Cloud readiness remains a separate slice; this PR does not turn the existing desktop bootstrap into cloud provisioning.

## Verification

All checks were rerun on the published head after the prior Mac-disconnect interruption. The abandoned disposable stack was cleaned and the original local app restored before the fresh run.

* Frozen install, Knope, formatting, lint and diff checks passed; three pre-existing lint warnings remain.
* 2,692 server + 1,707 app + 383 PostgreSQL + 275 functional/documentation browser tests passed: 5,057 total. Browser baseline completed in 3.3 minutes, with owned stack cleanup and original app restoration verified.
* Terraform formatting, all three roots and HIGH/CRITICAL config scanning passed.
* Linux/amd64 production build, runtime/size/source-map verification, SBOM and HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability scanning passed.
* Retained entrypoint/ignore checks and seven-worktree hook-removal assertions passed. Independent local review found no regression.
* Copilot reviewed exact head 6de30fa7a39 at 08:37:14 UTC November 8 and recommended approval with no actionable comments/unresolved threads. It skipped 18 deleted generated .idea files; those were checked locally. Review: [https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/209#pullrequestreview-5817220698](<https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/209#pullrequestreview-5817220698>) .
* Required remote CI, including CI/gate, passed on the same head: [https://github.com/evorto-app/app/actions/runs/42463471253](<https://github.com/evorto-app/app/actions/runs/42463471253>) . CodeQL and Copilot setup also passed; optional CodeRabbit skipped the draft.

## Optional follow-ups, not started

1. Refresh stale Effect skill advice (effect@beta / Context.Tag versus app Effect 4.0.6 / Context.Service), preferably upstream or a project override.
2. Pin Angular MCP to the app's CLI version instead of @latest.
3. Replace stale root references to absent e2e/\*\* and a machine-specific Effect path.
4. Review the large vendored-reference footprint while preserving reproducible/offline source verification.

entire trail — Manage trails across repositories and branches A trail captures project intent across repositories and branches. Manage intent and discussions on the whole trail; use --repo and --branch to select context for checkout, sessions, findings, and approvals. When to use this: Trail commands talk to entire.io and read the saved login from the OS keyring (the Keychain on macOS), so they need network and keyring access. If you run commands in a sandbox, request unsandboxed execution for `entire trail` up front. An error saying the Keychain is not accessible or the network is not allowed means the sandbox blocked it, not that the user is logged out: ask to re-run it unsandboxed, and do not run `entire login`. A project trail spans repositories; each change is its branch in one repository. Project trails and changes are numbered separately: never pass

where a change is expected, or where a project trail is. Pass / to checkout, resume, finding, watch, approvals or approve; given to show, it shows the parent project trail. Users paste Entire trail URLs. Do not pass a URL to any command; map the path after the host to a selector: //-/trails/

/changes// change / ///-/trails/

/changes/ change / ///trails/ change / //-/trails/

project trail

Add --project / unless is origin's owner. To link a trail or change, use the url `entire trail show` prints. Current repo: gh/evorto-app/app (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo) Flags: --project string Project as gh/ or et/; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace --repo string Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; for list, only filters the required --project Inherited flags: --context name Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them) Subcommands: approvals · approve · attachment · checkout · ci-pr · comment · create · finding · link · list · merge · ready · rerun-review · resume · retarget · sessions · show · stack · timeline · unlink · update · update-branch · watch read-only: approvals, list, sessions, show, stack, timeline, watch — others write Next: entire agent-help trail Show a repository: its identity, visibility, and one row per cluster it is placed on, with that cluster's clone URL and status. With no repository argument, resolve the current clone's origin remote. --json includes repoId and apiUrl for the responsible API cell when resolvable. A GitHub mirror whose owner refused the Entire app's access while syncing (an org IP allow list, or a suspension Entire hit mid-sync; a suspension GitHub reported directly shows as placement status suspended instead) shows a Sync section with the fix and the resync command; --json carries it as syncBlock. When that read fails the text view prints a note and --json sets syncStatus to "unavailable", so a missing syncBlock means not blocked only when syncStatus is absent. An explicit names its forge: - /et// — an Entire-native repo, shown with its primary cluster and each mirror of it, plus how far a seed in progress has got - /gh// — a GitHub upstream, shown with its mirror on every cluster - an entire:// clone URL, as `git clone` takes it. ## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly selected the existing GitHub mirror as the working flow, superseding the fresh-repository/new-initial-commit plan below. Use Entire Trails over `gh/evorto-app/app`; retain GitHub history, PRs and required checks during this phase. No repository recreation or ancestry reset is planned for this phase.

Codex in the current consolidation chat owns inventory and linking existing PR branches into Entire Trails. Initial inventory: PR208 Stripe webhook claim fencing and draft PR209 EVO-8 tooling cleanup; no open Trails existed. Mirror is ready in EU and US. Preserve both independent changes, existing reviews and exact heads. Verify Trail/PR association and report merge gates before changing readiness or merging. Keep required review/CI protections; no forced merges, deployments or subscription changes. Broader RWX migration remains separate under EVO-50.

Acceptance for this phase: both existing branches are accessible through Trails, linked PRs/checks and remaining gates are recorded, and the mirror-based daily workflow is concrete. The earlier fresh-repository criteria below are historical and superseded where they conflict.

patch.text:
## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas has now selected “Use the existing mirror” for the working flow, superseding the earlier new-initial-commit/fresh Entire repository decision below. EVO-54 is beginning PR consolidation into Entire Trails on the existing `gh/evorto-app/app` mirror while preserving GitHub history, PRs and required checks. Native hosting, RWX replacement and eventual GitHub retirement require later validation; they are not prerequisites for using Trails today. Do not recreate the repository or reset ancestry under the historical criteria below.

{"id":"EVO-50","uuid":"290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e","title":"Move Evorto to Entire and RWX with smaller workflows and reliable test selection","description":"## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas has now selected “Use the existing mirror” for the working flow, superseding the earlier new-initial-commit/fresh Entire repository decision below. <issue id="66c4077f-4104-439f-97bf-5a57f6a7dc79" label="EVO-54" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-54/migrate-git-hosting-and-protected-review-to-entire" /> is beginning PR consolidation into Entire Trails on the existing `gh/evorto-app/app` mirror while preserving GitHub history, PRs and required checks. Native hosting, RWX replacement and eventual GitHub retirement require later validation; they are not prerequisites for using Trails today. Do not recreate the repository or reset ancestry under the historical criteria below.

## Outcome

Host evorto-app/app natively on Entire and rebuild CI/CD on RWX. Replace oversized, repeated workflow setup with small tasks and an understandable test-selection interface shared by local agents and CI. Cancel the paid GitHub subscription after the replacement is proven.

The user selected RWX and is comfortable rebuilding jobs rather than preserving GitHub Actions YAML. Budget is small; determine actual GitHub savings and measure RWX usage rather than assuming either amount.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Scope

* Inventory current checks, integrations, protections, release automation, credentials and costs.
* Define named verification suites and conservative, explainable change-based selection.
* Rebuild quality, integration, browser and image verification as focused RWX tasks.
* Migrate Git hosting, review and required checks to Entire.
* Rebuild staging, release certification and production promotion.
* Validate coverage, reliability, cost and rollback before cutover and subscription cancellation.

## Existing evidence and coordination

Current workflows include Bun/Angular unit tests, PostgreSQL integration, Docker Compose with Playwright, Terraform checks, image/runtime verification, SBOM/vulnerability scans, provider certification and Scaleway deployment. GitHub-specific dependencies include environments, workflow chaining, gh API/release calls, Knope and PR tooling; audit current main and active branches before implementation.

<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> currently removes Entire hooks and Git Town requirements; <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> establishes PR-only publication and Linear-linked naming. Reconcile these with the new hosting direction without blindly reverting cleanup or losing protected review. Keep Linear tracking for this migration; migrating the wider issue backlog to Trails is a separate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

* Entire is the canonical Git remote, initialized from the agreed main snapshot as one new initial commit with no imported ancestry. Verify the snapshot against its recorded source SHA, preserve the old repository recoverably, and verify access, review and required-check protections.
* RWX runs the required suites and reports usable checks to Trails.
* Local and hosted verification use the same documented suite definitions and selection rules.
* Selection explains its decisions, supports a full run, and falls back to broad coverage for unknown/shared/high-risk changes. No skipped tests or reduced coverage are disguised as a complete run.
* Repeated setup and builds are shared where safe; deployment and live-provider checks execute fresh.
* Staging and production use the same verified image digest, with schema compatibility, serialization and explicit production approval preserved.
* A complete change-to-production trial, rollback procedure and measured cost are recorded before cutover.
* Cancel the verified GitHub subscription only after replacement readiness; preserve recoverable repository/archive data and check effects on other repositories.

## Execution

Complete the linked subissues in dependency order. This issue records the plan; creating it does not execute migrations, deployments or subscription changes.

Lukas explicitly selected the existing GitHub mirror as the working flow, superseding the fresh-repository/new-initial-commit plan below. ## Goal

Prepare Entire-native hosting and replace GitHub-specific review protections without losing recoverable work.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.
* Preserve the original repository, historical refs, pending local/remote work and agent history recoverably outside the new repository. Resolve or explicitly defer/carry/archive outstanding work before choosing the snapshot; do not lose work that has not reached main.
* Configure canonical remotes, access and review rules. Verify required approvals/checks and protections against bypass, accidental deletion and history rewriting.

* Document how Linear issues link to Trails/branches and how release tooling will work. Do not assume native Linear status sync exists.
* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

## Execution

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

## Codex

In 2025, Codex moved beyond being just a coding model and became your Software Engineer teammate: connecting models, local tooling, and cloud to help developers tackle longer, more complex coding tasks.

### Models

Early reasoning models demonstrated strong gains on complex coding tasks (multi-file edits, debugging, planning). By mid-late 2025, these capabilities were consolidated into the GPT-5 family, with GPT-5.2-Codex becoming the latest default choice for code generation, review, and repo-scale reasoning—no longer separate from general-purpose models, but specialized within them.

### CLI

The open-source Codex CLI (GitHub) brought agent-style coding directly into local environments, enabling developers to run Codex over real repositories, iteratively review changes, and apply edits to files with human oversight. This made long-horizon coding tasks practical in day-to-day workflows.

Codex also became easier to operationalize beyond interactive use, with built-in support for repeatable automation patterns like scripting Codex.

### Safety, control, and integrations

Codex leaned into the realities of shipping: sandboxing and approval modes made it easier to keep humans in the loop. At the same time, support for AGENTS.md and MCP made Codex easier to adapt to your repo, extend with third-party tools and context, and even orchestrate Codex via the Agents SDK (by running the CLI as an MCP server).

Update, September 5, 2026: The Codex MCP server has been removed. See the migration guidance for current integration options.

### Web, cloud, and IDE

Beyond the CLI, Codex expanded support for longer sessions and iterative problem solving across the web + cloud and the IDE extension, tightening the loop between conversational reasoning and concrete code changes. Teams could also automate parts of the workflow with Codex Autofix in CI.

Why it matters: by the end of 2025, Codex functioned less as “a model you prompt” and more as a coding surface–combining reasoning-capable models with tools developers already use.

The Agents API gives your application access to the Codex harness through an OpenAI-managed API.

OpenAI manages sessions, orchestration, context compaction, and recovery while your application provides tools and chooses its execution environment.

Agents can operate in a sandbox where they can execute code, edit files, connect to MCP servers, and produce artifacts.

See the API reference for endpoints, request parameters, and response fields.

## Pricing

Model usage is billed at the selected model’s API rates. OpenAI tools use their standard rates, and OpenAI-hosted sandboxes use standard container rates.

## Try an example

Try these complete examples:

  * Create and run a directory-tree script in an OpenAI-hosted sandbox.
  * Compare release notes with subagents and combine their findings into one answer.

Explore complete applications:

  * Incident response agent: investigate alerts and request approval for recovery actions.

Yes—the existing mirror looks like the better route for your setup.

**Trails combine planning and code review:** a Trail can begin as an issue with no code, then contain one or more branch changes. On a GitHub mirror, those changes use linked GitHub PRs for CI and merging. Entire approvals remain separate from GitHub approvals. [Entire’s explanation](https://entire.com/blog/how-to-run-custom-ai-code-evals-on-every-push-with-trails)

I’ve already connected both open PRs:

| Change | Entire |
|---|---|
| #208 — Stripe webhook fix | [Trail 1](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1) |
| #209 — Tooling cleanup | [Trail 2](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2) |

Both retain their existing commits, PRs and checks. Neither has been merged.

For issues, I recommend migrating active work into intent-only Trails first, preserving Linear identifiers and source links. We should verify how dependencies, statuses and discussion history map before moving the whole backlog.

The next concrete step is configuring Entire’s review gates—they’re currently disabled—then updating the repository’s agent instructions for the Trail workflow. I’ve recorded your mirror decision and these remaining steps in [EVO-54](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-54/migrate-git-hosting-and-protected-review-to-entire).
