{"id":"EVO-54","uuid":"66c4077f-4104-439f-97bf-5a57f6a7dc79","title":"Migrate Git hosting and protected review to Entire","description":"## Expanded authorized scope — 8 November 2026

Lukas requested collaborator onboarding to Entire and shared repository instructions/configuration for Codex, Claude and Gemini/Antigravity (tool name clarification pending), with all workflow changes recorded. Codex will prepare a reviewable child change above PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> so the earlier cleanup cannot erase the new agent entrypoints. Shared AGENTS.md remains canonical; thin tool-specific entrypoints direct agents to the same Trail workflow. Do not re-enable optional transcript recording without resolving that separate choice. Verify against installed CLI and official tool instruction-loading documentation; run lint/format after edits and validate paths/config. Preserve application behavior and full publication gates.

Constraint discovered: installed CLI states that GitHub mirror repository access follows GitHub upstream and grants are read-only in Entire; moving collaborator daily work to Entire does not decouple repository authorization from GitHub. Record this explicitly, preserve current access until the replacement is verified, and use native hosting as a later distinct decision if independent Entire access is required. Do not remove collaborators from GitHub on the assumption that the mirror has independent grants.

## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly selected the existing GitHub mirror as the working flow, superseding the fresh-repository/new-initial-commit plan below. Use Entire Trails over `gh/evorto-app/app`; retain GitHub history, PRs and required checks during this phase. No repository recreation or ancestry reset is planned for this phase.

Codex in the current consolidation chat owns inventory and linking existing PR branches into Entire Trails. Initial inventory: PR208 Stripe webhook claim fencing and draft PR209 <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> tooling cleanup; no open Trails existed. Mirror is ready in EU and US. Preserve both independent changes, existing reviews and exact heads. Verify Trail/PR association and report merge gates before changing readiness or merging. Keep required review/CI protections; no forced merges, deployments or subscription changes. Broader RWX migration remains separate under <issue id="290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e" label="EVO-50" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test" />.

Acceptance for this phase: both existing branches are accessible through Trails, linked PRs/checks and remaining gates are recorded, and the mirror-based daily workflow is concrete. The earlier fresh-repository criteria below are historical and superseded where they conflict.

## Goal

Prepare Entire-native hosting and replace GitHub-specific review protections without losing recoverable work.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.
* Preserve the original repository, historical refs, pending local/remote work and agent history recoverably outside the new repository. Resolve or explicitly defer/carry/archive outstanding work before choosing the snapshot; do not lose work that has not reached main.
* Configure canonical remotes, access and review rules. Verify required approvals/checks and protections against bypass, accidental deletion and history rewriting.
* Install/connect RWX and verify commit/Trail checks and failure blocking. Audit integration limitations rather than assuming GitHub feature parity.
* Reconcile <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> cleanup and <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> publication guidance; configure only required Entire tooling and update local-agent instructions.
* Document how Linear issues link to Trails/branches and how release tooling will work. Do not assume native Linear status sync exists.
* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

## Execution

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

## Consolidation verified — 8 November 2026

Created Entire Trail 1 for PR208: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1>) and Trail 2 for PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" />: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2>) . `entire trail ci-pr` returned the existing PR numbers 208 and 209; no replacement PRs or code pushes were needed. Exact heads remain 914f2d9b2ca7d03a0445ba958550712d6afc853e and 6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd. Both show CI/gate success and clean conflicts. PR208 is one commit behind main; PR209 is up to date. Read-only merge dry runs say mergeable, but all four Entire gates (approvals, checks, findings, up_to_date) are disabled. Dry-run success is therefore not proof of equivalent GitHub protection or release readiness. No merge or readiness change performed.

Working flow: retain GitHub origin; create a Trail linked to a feature branch; use ci-pr to link/create its GitHub PR for checks; inspect Trail checks/findings and GitHub review requirements; merge only after required local verification and both platforms' applicable gates. Entire approvals and GitHub approvals are separate. Optional session recording is independent.

Open decisions: whether/how to migrate the Linear backlog into intent-only Trails (titles, bodies, owners, priorities and source links can be represented, but preserving dependency/status/comment history needs an explicit migration design); configure and validate Entire gates; reconcile checked-in agent workflow guidance through a separate reviewed change. Linear remains the canonical issue tracker under current repository policy until that policy is deliberately changed. patch.text:
## Confirmed direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly wants to cancel the paid GitHub organization subscription after the migration and move collaborators' daily workflow to Entire. Keep the GitHub organization/repository and mirror integration on the appropriate free plan; subscription downgrade is distinct from deleting the organization or removing repository collaborators. Audit actual plan, renewal, other repositories, seats, usage/storage and feature losses before executing. Public/private repository protection and collaborator access must remain functional. GitHub-backed Entire mirror permissions remain upstream GitHub permissions, so Entire UI adoption alone does not eliminate that access dependency. Do not promise that plan cancellation eliminates Actions/storage/add-on charges.

{"id":"EVO-57","uuid":"57ccf8be-84d5-48db-9781-ea1183952dd2","title":"Cancel the paid GitHub subscription after verified cutover","description":"## Confirmed direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly wants to cancel the paid GitHub organization subscription after the migration and move collaborators' daily workflow to Entire. Keep the GitHub organization/repository and mirror integration on the appropriate free plan; subscription downgrade is distinct from deleting the organization or removing repository collaborators. Audit actual plan, renewal, other repositories, seats, usage/storage and feature losses before executing. Public/private repository protection and collaborator access must remain functional. GitHub-backed Entire mirror permissions remain upstream GitHub permissions, so Entire UI adoption alone does not eliminate that access dependency. Do not promise that plan cancellation eliminates Actions/storage/add-on charges.

## Goal

Realize the verified GitHub savings once Entire and RWX are operating successfully.

## Acceptance criteria

* Recheck the exact subscription/account, renewal date, remaining usage/storage charges and effects on other repositories or users. Cancel the intended paid product only.
* Confirm validation is complete and required hosting, checks, reviews, releases and deployment capabilities no longer depend on paid GitHub features.
* Preserve an agreed recoverable archive, Git history, issue/PR/release references and necessary non-secret records. Do not delete the repository or account as part of cancellation.

  services, environment variables, or credentials are blockers to resolve, not
  reasons to defer coverage to CI. CI confirms an already-green local result;
  it is never the first full test run.
- After every file edit, run `bun run lint` and `bun run format:write`.
- Lint covers application, test, helper, and root TypeScript config sources
  while excluding vendored `repos/`. Node-side helper/config tooling uses the
  shared TypeScript correctness rules without Angular UI or deterministic
  sort-order rules.
- Markdown-only edits do not need a WebStorm `get_file_problems` pass.
- Before calling WebStorm `get_file_problems` on edited files, run `bun run lint`.
- After editing non-Markdown files, run WebStorm `get_file_problems` on those files when possible.
- Prefer sequential `get_file_problems` checks; parallel runs can time out.
- For UI behavior changes, use Browser verification where useful and add/update Playwright coverage for durable behavior.
- For generated documentation flows, keep Playwright docs current.
- See `QUALITY.md` for done criteria and Browser/Playwright guidance.

## Conventions

- TypeScript strict mode is enforced.
- Indentation: 2 spaces.
- Filenames: `kebab-case.ts`.
- Symbols: `camelCase` and `PascalCase`.
- Prefer path aliases: `@app/*`, `@server/*`, `@db/*`, `@shared/*`, `@helpers/*`.
- Import `src/types/**` directly; TypeScript reserves the `@types/*` package
  namespace and rejects that path form in production builds.
- For Effect reference and usage patterns, consult the local Effect source at `/Users/hedde/code/effect` when behavior or recommended composition is unclear.

## Commit, PR, and Release Notes

- Use feature branches and GitHub PRs; do not push changes directly to `main`.
- Fetch and inspect the current base before starting work and before proposing
  review. Preserve uncommitted work and coordinate overlapping branches.
- Use ordinary Git and the GitHub CLI or website for branch and PR management.
- For multi-phase work, use [GitHub stacked PRs](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-pull-requests)
  with one reviewable branch per phase. The optional `gh stack` extension can
  manage local stacks; keep each PR based on its immediate predecessor.
- Request Copilot review on every PR and address actionable comments before
  treating the reviewed head as ready.
- Commit messages should be imperative and concise.
- PRs should include purpose, scope, schema/runtime impact, and UI evidence where relevant.
- Every PR needs a new Knope change file in `.changeset/*.md`, including
  test-only and CI-only changes. The hosted Knope Bot enforces this requirement.
- Before starting full verification, check that the PR diff includes its change
  file. `knope --validate` checks configuration and file validity; it does not
  check whether the current PR adds a change file.

script = '''
set -euo pipefail

SOURCE_ROOT=${CODEX_SOURCE_ROOT:-$(pwd -P)}

echo "[setup] Refreshing git branch content"
if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
    echo "[setup] Worktree has local changes; skipping branch refresh."
  else
    CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD || true)
    SOURCE_BRANCH=""
    if [ -d "$SOURCE_ROOT/.git" ] || git -C "$SOURCE_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      SOURCE_BRANCH=$(git -C "$SOURCE_ROOT" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD || true)
    fi
    TARGET_BRANCH=${CURRENT_BRANCH:-$SOURCE_BRANCH}

    if [ -n "$TARGET_BRANCH" ]; then
      git fetch --quiet origin "$TARGET_BRANCH" || true
      TARGET_REF=$TARGET_BRANCH
      if git rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/$TARGET_BRANCH" >/dev/null; then
        TARGET_REF=origin/$TARGET_BRANCH
      fi

      if [ -n "$CURRENT_BRANCH" ]; then
        git merge --ff-only "$TARGET_REF"
      else
        git checkout --detach "$TARGET_REF"
      fi
    else
      echo "[setup] Could not infer a source branch; skipping branch refresh."

  fi
fi

if [ "$(pwd -P)" != "$SOURCE_ROOT" ]; then

# Rules

Section titled “Rules”

Rules are manually defined constraints for the Agent to follow, at both the local and global levels. Rules allow users to guide the agent to follow behaviors particular to their own use cases and style.

To get started with Rules:

  1. Open the Customizations panel via the ”…” dropdown at the top of the editor’s agent panel.
  2. Navigate to the Rules panel.
  3. Click + Global to create new Global Rules, or + Workspace to create new Workspace-specific rules.

A Rule itself is simply a Markdown file, where you can input the constraints to guide the Agent to your tasks, stack, and style.

Rules files are limited to 12,000 characters each.

## Global Rules

Section titled “Global Rules”

Global rules live in ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md and are applied across all workspaces.

## Workspace Rules

Section titled “Workspace Rules”

Workspace rules live in the .agents/rules folder of your workspace or git root.

At the rule level you can define how a rule should be activated:

  * Manual: The rule is manually activated via at mention in Agent’s input box.
  * Always On: The rule is always applied.
  * Model Decision: Based on a natural language description of the rule, the model decides whether to apply the rule.
  * Glob: Based on the glob pattern you define (e.g., .js, src/**/.ts), the rule will be applied to all files that match the pattern.

Note: Antigravity now defaults to .agents/rules, but still maintains backward support for .agent/rules.

## @ Mentions

Section titled “@ Mentions”

You can reference other files using @filename in a Rules file. If filename is a relative path, it will be interpreted relative to the location of the Rules file. If filename is an absolute path, it will be resolved as a true absolute path, otherwise it will be resolved relative to the repository. For example, @/path/to/file.md will first attempt to be resolved to /path/to/file.md, and if that file does not exist, it will be resolved to workspace/path/to/file.md.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For files you edit, also read the nearest module `AGENTS.md` and README.
Shared project skills live in `.agents/skills`.
# AI tooling

Codex and Claude are the supported development assistants.

- `AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guide. Read the nearest module
  `AGENTS.md` and README for local rules.
- `CLAUDE.md` imports that same guide rather than maintaining a second manual.
- `.codex/config.toml` configures Codex MCP servers and features.
- `.codex/environments/environment.toml` configures Codex worktree setup.
- `.agents/skills` contains reusable skills. Update third-party skills together
  with `skills-lock.json`; keep project-specific adaptations separate.
- `.github/workflows/copilot-code-review.yml` supports the required Copilot PR
  review. It does not configure a separate development agent or require private
  packages and runtime credentials.

Keep shared formatting and linting in `.editorconfig`, Prettier, and ESLint
configuration rather than checking in editor-specific settings.

are separate from Entire Git hosting. The planned hosting and CI migration is
tracked in [EVO-50](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test);

      access. Record evidence without copying tokens or private session data.

- [ ] Reconcile EVO-8 cleanup and EVO-9 PR-only policy with Trail publication;
      preserve no-direct-main rules and required review during the transition.
- [ ] Configure Entire review agents and gates, including exact-head/stale
      review behavior; test that failures block merging. Confirm GitHub's
      upstream rules independently. Mirror protection is owned by GitHub.
- [ ] Inventory Linear issues and map each to a canonical Trail, preserving EVO
      IDs, source links, owners, priorities, acceptance criteria and dependencies.
      Preserve comment/status history in a recoverable export or linked source.
      Pilot one issue, reconcile counts and ownership, then migrate remaining
      work. Do not close/delete source issues until verification. No automatic
      Linear/Entire status synchronization is assumed.

Lukas wants to cancel the paid organization subscription after migration,
retaining the organization and mirrored repository on an appropriate free plan.

public repositories; private-repository feature loss and organization-wide

* Remove five root tool/editor config folders: .air, .gemini, .entire, .idea and .vscode. Remove optional Entire recording hooks and Copilot cloud-agent setup.

No invitations, access removal, billing change, merge or deployment occurred.

## Expanded authorized scope — 8 November 2026

Lukas requested collaborator onboarding to Entire and shared repository instructions/configuration for Codex, Claude and Gemini/Antigravity (tool name clarification pending), with all workflow changes recorded. Codex will prepare a reviewable child change above PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> so the earlier cleanup cannot erase the new agent entrypoints. Shared AGENTS.md remains canonical; thin tool-specific entrypoints direct agents to the same Trail workflow. Do not re-enable optional transcript recording without resolving that separate choice. Verify against installed CLI and official tool instruction-loading documentation; run lint/format after edits and validate paths/config. Preserve application behavior and full publication gates.

Constraint discovered: installed CLI states that GitHub mirror repository access follows GitHub upstream and grants are read-only in Entire; moving collaborator daily work to Entire does not decouple repository authorization from GitHub. Record this explicitly, preserve current access until the replacement is verified, and use native hosting as a later distinct decision if independent Entire access is required. Do not remove collaborators from GitHub on the assumption that the mirror has independent grants.

## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly selected the existing GitHub mirror as the working flow, superseding the fresh-repository/new-initial-commit plan below. Use Entire Trails over `gh/evorto-app/app`; retain GitHub history, PRs and required checks during this phase. No repository recreation or ancestry reset is planned for this phase.

Codex in the current consolidation chat owns inventory and linking existing PR branches into Entire Trails. Initial inventory: PR208 Stripe webhook claim fencing and draft PR209 <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> tooling cleanup; no open Trails existed. Mirror is ready in EU and US. Preserve both independent changes, existing reviews and exact heads. Verify Trail/PR association and report merge gates before changing readiness or merging. Keep required review/CI protections; no forced merges, deployments or subscription changes. Broader RWX migration remains separate under <issue id="290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e" label="EVO-50" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test" />.

Acceptance for this phase: both existing branches are accessible through Trails, linked PRs/checks and remaining gates are recorded, and the mirror-based daily workflow is concrete. The earlier fresh-repository criteria below are historical and superseded where they conflict.

## Goal

Prepare Entire-native hosting and replace GitHub-specific review protections without losing recoverable work.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.
* Preserve the original repository, historical refs, pending local/remote work and agent history recoverably outside the new repository. Resolve or explicitly defer/carry/archive outstanding work before choosing the snapshot; do not lose work that has not reached main.
* Configure canonical remotes, access and review rules. Verify required approvals/checks and protections against bypass, accidental deletion and history rewriting.
* Install/connect RWX and verify commit/Trail checks and failure blocking. Audit integration limitations rather than assuming GitHub feature parity.
* Reconcile <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> cleanup and <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> publication guidance; configure only required Entire tooling and update local-agent instructions.
* Document how Linear issues link to Trails/branches and how release tooling will work. Do not assume native Linear status sync exists.
* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

## Execution

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

## Consolidation verified — 8 November 2026

Created Entire Trail 1 for PR208: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1>) and Trail 2 for PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" />: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2>) . `entire trail ci-pr` returned the existing PR numbers 208 and 209; no replacement PRs or code pushes were needed. Exact heads remain 914f2d9b2ca7d03a0445ba958550712d6afc853e and 6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd. Both show CI/gate success and clean conflicts. PR208 is one commit behind main; PR209 is up to date. Read-only merge dry runs say mergeable, but all four Entire gates (approvals, checks, findings, up_to_date) are disabled. Dry-run success is therefore not proof of equivalent GitHub protection or release readiness. No merge or readiness change performed.

Working flow: retain GitHub origin; create a Trail linked to a feature branch; use ci-pr to link/create its GitHub PR for checks; inspect Trail checks/findings and GitHub review requirements; merge only after required local verification and both platforms' applicable gates. Entire approvals and GitHub approvals are separate. Optional session recording is independent.

Open decisions: whether/how to migrate the Linear backlog into intent-only Trails (titles, bodies, owners, priorities and source links can be represented, but preserving dependency/status/comment history needs an explicit migration design); configure and validate Entire gates; reconcile checked-in agent workflow guidance through a separate reviewed change. Linear remains the canonical issue tracker under current repository policy until that policy is deliberately changed. # Entire operating workflow and migration

Owner: EVO-54 under EVO-50. Billing: EVO-57. This document records current
operation and remaining migration work; unchecked items are not shipped.

## Current operation

Use Entire Trails over the existing GitHub mirror `gh/evorto-app/app`.
Keep `origin` pointed at GitHub during this phase. Preserve Git history,
outstanding work and PR reviews. The earlier plan to create a repository with
one new initial commit is superseded.

A Trail records intent before code exists and can contain several branch
changes. Each change has its own base, review and merge. On this mirror it uses
a linked GitHub PR for CI and merging. Entire approvals are separate from
GitHub approvals. Linear remains the issue source of truth until the migration
below is verified and repository policy changes land.

Read the installed CLI's `entire agent-help` before using it. In particular:

```sh
entire repo view --json
entire trail list --project gh/evorto-app --status open --json
entire agent-help trail create
entire agent-help trail link
entire agent-help trail ci-pr
entire agent-help trail show
entire agent-help trail finding
entire agent-help trail merge
```

For planning, `entire trail create --no-branch` creates intent without publishing
code. For existing remote work, explicit `--repo gh/evorto-app/app` with
`--branch <existing-branch>` and `--base <actual-base>` links that branch without
pushing a local checkout. Inspect existing work first to avoid duplicate Trails.
`entire trail ci-pr <repository/change>` links or creates the supporting PR;
verify it reused the intended PR. These operations can trigger automation, so
complete required local verification before publishing any new code.

Use `entire trail show <trail> --project gh/evorto-app --json` to inspect the
changes and exact heads. Use the returned change URL and repository/change
selector, not an assumed equality between Trail, change and GitHub PR numbers.
Check both platforms' approvals, findings, required checks and base freshness.
`entire trail merge <repository/change> --dry-run --json` is a read-only preview;
it neither approves the change nor proves GitHub will accept a real merge.
Never use `--force` to get through migration.

Initial consolidation on 8 November 2026:

| GitHub work                                                                 | Entire change                                                               | Observed state                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| [PR208](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/208), Stripe webhook fencing | [Trail 1, app/1](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1) | CI/gate passed; one commit behind main |
| [PR209](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/209), EVO-8 tooling cleanup  | [Trail 2, app/2](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2) | CI/gate passed; draft PR; up to date   |

These are dated observations, not standing approval. All four inspected Entire
gates (approvals, checks, findings, up_to_date) were disabled. Recheck current
state before any publication or merge. This configuration change is based on
PR209 so its removal of old tool folders cannot overwrite the new entrypoints.

## Agent entrypoints

All agents must read root and nearest module guidance, not maintain parallel
copies of repository policy. Codex reads `AGENTS.md`; Claude uses `CLAUDE.md`;
Gemini CLI uses `GEMINI.md`; current Antigravity supports `AGENTS.md` and
`GEMINI.md`. Tool settings should contain only required, portable configuration.
Authentication, workspace trust and personal permissions remain local.

Optional Entire session/checkpoint capture is independent of Trails. Do not
restore old hooks merely to use hosting or code review. If recording is adopted
later, verify supported agents against the installed CLI and review where
checkpoint data is uploaded, especially for this public repository. Do not
commit credentials or transcript caches.

## Collaborator transition

Move daily planning, review and handoffs to Entire. A GitHub mirror's repository
permissions still come from GitHub; `entire repo grant add/remove` cannot assign
independent permissions on this mirror. Keep the GitHub grants while using it.
Independent Entire access requires a later native-hosting decision.

GitHub currently lists `heddendorp` (admin), `FranzZehetleitner` and
`laurenskuchta` (write). Entire's mirror grant listing currently returns only
`github:heddendorp`. That does not establish why the others are absent or prove
their access. Each collaborator must authenticate and verify access before any
access changes. Do not send invitations or messages without explicit direction.

- [ ] Verify each collaborator can sign in, find the repo/Trails, pull/push a
      feature branch, review and see checks with their own identity.
- [ ] Agree owner/admin/reviewer responsibilities and test denied operations.
- [ ] Verify offboarding and account recovery; retain an owner with recovery
      access. Record evidence without copying tokens or private session data.

## Remaining workflow changes

- [ ] Reconcile EVO-8 cleanup and EVO-9 PR-only policy with Trail publication;
      preserve no-direct-main rules and required review during the transition.
- [ ] Configure Entire review agents and gates, including exact-head/stale
      review behavior; test that failures block merging. Confirm GitHub's
      upstream rules independently. Mirror protection is owned by GitHub.
- [ ] Inventory Linear issues and map each to a canonical Trail, preserving EVO
      IDs, source links, owners, priorities, acceptance criteria and dependencies.
      Preserve comment/status history in a recoverable export or linked source.
      Pilot one issue, reconcile counts and ownership, then migrate remaining
      work. Do not close/delete source issues until verification. No automatic
      Linear/Entire status synchronization is assumed.
- [ ] Update AGENTS.md's issue-first/naming rules after the issue cutover;
      make new planning and progress records authoritative in one place.
- [ ] Define shared local/CI suites and conservative test selection (EVO-52).
      Rebuild verification on RWX (EVO-53); retain complete coverage and local
      pre-publication verification, including browser/provider requirements.
- [ ] Replace GitHub-dependent release, Knope/change-file, artifact/image,
      documentation and deployment integration where needed (EVO-55). Preserve
      schema compatibility, identical image digests, secret boundaries,
      serialization, production approval and rollback.
- [ ] Verify Codex cloud/review and all agent entrypoints using the mirror;
      local CLI access alone does not prove cloud integration readiness.
- [ ] Trial failure blocking, stale heads, collaborator access, independent
      recovery and an authorized release before declaring cutover (EVO-56).
- [ ] Disable duplicate CI only after replacement evidence. Remove obsolete
      tokens/integrations only after verifying their remaining consumers.

## GitHub subscription and cost

Lukas wants to cancel the paid organization subscription after migration,
retaining the organization and mirrored repository on an appropriate free plan.
This is a plan downgrade, not deletion or collaborator revocation.

On 8 November 2026 GitHub's organization API reported plan `enterprise`, one
filled seat, one public repository and no private repositories. That is not an
invoice or verified renewal date. GitHub Free supports protected branches for
public repositories; private-repository feature loss and organization-wide
effects must still be checked against the actual account and billing screen.

- [ ] Verify the billing owner, actual product, enterprise relationship, renewal,
      downgrade effective date, other repositories and feature losses.
- [ ] Check seats, Actions, storage, packages and separately billed add-ons.
      A free organization plan does not imply zero usage/add-on charges.
- [ ] Record current cost and projected remaining GitHub + Entire/RWX cost;
      set available usage controls without inventing savings.
- [ ] Complete the migration validation, execute the intended downgrade and
      verify its effective date and billing state (EVO-57).

## References

- [Entire Trails and GitHub-backed CI/merging](https://entire.com/blog/how-to-run-custom-ai-code-evals-on-every-push-with-trails)
- Installed `entire agent-help` and `entire repo grant list --help` for current
  command behavior and mirror authorization.
- [Gemini context files](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/)
- [Antigravity rules](https://antigravity.google/docs/rules/)
- [GitHub protected branches](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)
- [GitHub plan downgrade](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/how-tos/manage-plan-and-licenses/downgrade-plan)

Lukas requested collaborator onboarding to Entire and shared repository instructions/configuration for Codex, Claude and Gemini/Antigravity (tool name clarification pending), with all workflow changes recorded. ## Goal

Prepare Entire-native hosting and replace GitHub-specific review protections without losing recoverable work.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.
* Preserve the original repository, historical refs, pending local/remote work and agent history recoverably outside the new repository. Resolve or explicitly defer/carry/archive outstanding work before choosing the snapshot; do not lose work that has not reached main.
* Configure canonical remotes, access and review rules. Verify required approvals/checks and protections against bypass, accidental deletion and history rewriting.
* Install/connect RWX and verify commit/Trail checks and failure blocking. Audit integration limitations rather than assuming GitHub feature parity.
* Reconcile <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> cleanup and <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> publication guidance; configure only required Entire tooling and update local-agent instructions.
* Document how Linear issues link to Trails/branches and how release tooling will work. Do not assume native Linear status sync exists.
* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

# Entire operating workflow and migration

Owner: EVO-54 under EVO-50. Billing: EVO-57. This document records current
operation and remaining migration work; unchecked items are not shipped.

## Current operation

Use Entire Trails over the existing GitHub mirror `gh/evorto-app/app`.
Keep `origin` pointed at GitHub during this phase. Preserve Git history,
outstanding work and PR reviews. The earlier plan to create a repository with
one new initial commit is superseded.

A Trail records intent before code exists and can contain several branch
changes. Each change has its own base, review and merge. On this mirror it uses
a linked GitHub PR for CI and merging. Entire approvals are separate from
GitHub approvals. Linear remains the issue source of truth until the migration
below is verified and repository policy changes land.

Read the installed CLI's `entire agent-help` before using it. In particular:

```sh
entire repo view --json
entire trail list --project gh/evorto-app --status open --json
entire agent-help trail create
entire agent-help trail link
entire agent-help trail ci-pr
entire agent-help trail show
entire agent-help trail finding
entire agent-help trail merge
```

For planning, `entire trail create --no-branch` creates intent without publishing
code. For existing remote work, explicit `--repo gh/evorto-app/app` with
`--branch <existing-branch>` and `--base <actual-base>` links that branch without
pushing a local checkout. Inspect existing work first to avoid duplicate Trails.
`entire trail ci-pr <repository/change>` links or creates the supporting PR;
verify it reused the intended PR. These operations can trigger automation, so
complete required local verification before publishing any new code.

Use `entire trail show <trail> --project gh/evorto-app --json` to inspect the
changes and exact heads. Use the returned change URL and repository/change
selector, not an assumed equality between Trail, change and GitHub PR numbers.
Check both platforms' approvals, findings, required checks and base freshness.
`entire trail merge <repository/change> --dry-run --json` is a read-only preview;
it neither approves the change nor proves GitHub will accept a real merge.
Never use `--force` to get through migration.

Initial consolidation on 8 November 2026:

| GitHub work                                                                 | Entire change                                                               | Observed state                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| [PR208](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/208), Stripe webhook fencing | [Trail 1, app/1](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1) | CI/gate passed; one commit behind main |
| [PR209](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/209), EVO-8 tooling cleanup  | [Trail 2, app/2](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2) | CI/gate passed; draft PR; up to date   |

These are dated observations, not standing approval. All four inspected Entire
gates (approvals, checks, findings, up_to_date) were disabled. Recheck current
state before any publication or merge. This configuration change is based on
PR209 so its removal of old tool folders cannot overwrite the new entrypoints.

## Agent entrypoints

All agents must read root and nearest module guidance, not maintain parallel
copies of repository policy. Codex reads `AGENTS.md`; Claude uses `CLAUDE.md`;
Gemini CLI uses `GEMINI.md`; current Antigravity supports `AGENTS.md` and
`GEMINI.md`. Tool settings should contain only required, portable configuration.
Authentication, workspace trust and personal permissions remain local.

Optional Entire session/checkpoint capture is independent of Trails. Do not
restore old hooks merely to use hosting or code review. If recording is adopted
later, verify supported agents against the installed CLI and review where
checkpoint data is uploaded, especially for this public repository. Do not
commit credentials or transcript caches.

## Collaborator transition

Move daily planning, review and handoffs to Entire. A GitHub mirror's repository
permissions still come from GitHub; `entire repo grant add/remove` cannot assign
independent permissions on this mirror. Keep the GitHub grants while using it.
Independent Entire access requires a later native-hosting decision.

GitHub currently lists `heddendorp` (admin), `FranzZehetleitner` and
`laurenskuchta` (write). Entire's mirror grant listing currently returns only
`github:heddendorp`. That does not establish why the others are absent or prove
their access. Each collaborator must authenticate and verify access before any
access changes. Do not send invitations or messages without explicit direction.

- [ ] Verify each collaborator can sign in, find the repo/Trails, pull/push a
      feature branch, review and see checks with their own identity.
- [ ] Agree owner/admin/reviewer responsibilities and test denied operations.
- [ ] Verify offboarding and account recovery; retain an owner with recovery
      access. Record evidence without copying tokens or private session data.

## Remaining workflow changes

- [ ] Reconcile EVO-8 cleanup and EVO-9 PR-only policy with Trail publication;
      preserve no-direct-main rules and required review during the transition.
- [ ] Configure Entire review agents and gates, including exact-head/stale
      review behavior; test that failures block merging. Confirm GitHub's
      upstream rules independently. Mirror protection is owned by GitHub.
- [ ] Inventory Linear issues and map each to a canonical Trail, preserving EVO
      IDs, source links, owners, priorities, acceptance criteria and dependencies.
      Preserve comment/status history in a recoverable export or linked source.
      Pilot one issue, reconcile counts and ownership, then migrate remaining
      work. Do not close/delete source issues until verification. No automatic
      Linear/Entire status synchronization is assumed.
- [ ] Update AGENTS.md's issue-first/naming rules after the issue cutover;
      make new planning and progress records authoritative in one place.
- [ ] Define shared local/CI suites and conservative test selection (EVO-52).
      Rebuild verification on RWX (EVO-53); retain complete coverage and local
      pre-publication verification, including browser/provider requirements.
- [ ] Replace GitHub-dependent release, Knope/change-file, artifact/image,
      documentation and deployment integration where needed (EVO-55). Preserve
      schema compatibility, identical image digests, secret boundaries,
      serialization, production approval and rollback.
- [ ] Verify Codex cloud/review and all agent entrypoints using the mirror;
      local CLI access alone does not prove cloud integration readiness.
- [ ] Trial failure blocking, stale heads, collaborator access, independent
      recovery and an authorized release before declaring cutover (EVO-56).
- [ ] Disable duplicate CI only after replacement evidence. Remove obsolete
      tokens/integrations only after verifying their remaining consumers.

## GitHub subscription and cost

Lukas wants to cancel the paid organization subscription after migration,
retaining the organization and mirrored repository on an appropriate free plan.
This is a plan downgrade, not deletion or collaborator revocation.

On 8 November 2026 GitHub's organization API reported plan `enterprise`, one
filled seat, one public repository and no private repositories. That is not an
invoice or verified renewal date. GitHub Free supports protected branches for
public repositories; private-repository feature loss and organization-wide
effects must still be checked against the actual account and billing screen.

- [ ] Verify the billing owner, actual product, enterprise relationship, renewal,
      downgrade effective date, other repositories and feature losses.
- [ ] Check seats, Actions, storage, packages and separately billed add-ons.
      A free organization plan does not imply zero usage/add-on charges.
- [ ] Record current cost and projected remaining GitHub + Entire/RWX cost;
      set available usage controls without inventing savings.
- [ ] Complete the migration validation, execute the intended downgrade and
      verify its effective date and billing state (EVO-57).

citeturn7search0 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Plugin-bundled hooks are non-managed hooks, so Codex skips them until the user reviews and trusts the current hook definition. ...           "hooks": ["./hooks/session.json", "./hooks/tools.json"]
If you already have a plugin folder, you can still use `@plugin-creator` to wire it into a local marketplace.

### Plugin creator output

The current scaffold uses the Codex compatibility layout, not the portable Agent Plugins layout. When you request all optional components, it can create:
    
    `my-plugin/
    ├── .codex-plugin/
    │   └── plugin.json
    ├── .mcp.json
    ├── .app.json
    ├── skills/
    ├── hooks/
    ├── scripts/
    └── assets/`

Only `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is always created. The other files and directories are optional. `.mcp.json` starts with an empty `mcpServers` object, and `.app.json` starts with an empty `apps` object. The manifest references these files when requested. It also declares `skills: "./skills/"`; add your skill folders there before testing a skills-based plugin.

Requesting hooks creates an empty `hooks/` directory, not a hook configuration or executable script. Add `hooks/hooks.json` and its scripts using the bundled hooks guidance.

The scaffold remains supported. To author a portable package, follow Create a plugin manually and use root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` with their Agent Plugins schemas. Don’t just rename `.mcp.json`: the portable MCP format also declares a transport `type` for each server.


Codex discovers `hooks/hooks.json` by default when the selected OpenAI extension or compatibility manifest doesn’t define `hooks`:
    
    `{
      "hooks": {
        "SessionStart": [
          {
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/session_start.py",
                "statusMessage": "Loading plugin context"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }`

To override that default, define `hooks` inside `extensions.com.openai` in root `plugin.json`. The field can be a single path, an array of paths, an inline hooks object, or an array of inline hooks objects. An explicit value replaces default-file discovery; it doesn’t add to `hooks/hooks.json`.
    
    `{
      "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
      "name": "repo-policy",
      "extensions": {
        "com.openai": {
          "hooks": ["./hooks/session.json", "./hooks/tools.json"]
        }
      }
    }`

Legacy packages can declare `hooks` directly in `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.

## Environment

Each external-command invocation receives:

Variable  | Description
--- | ---
`ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`  | The CLI's version string (e.g. `0.42.0`, `dev`)
`ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`  | Absolute path to the git repository root, when the CLI is invoked inside one. Omitted otherwise.
`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`  | Per-plugin durable storage directory (`<plugin-root>/data/<name>`). Not pre-created — the plugin should `mkdir -p` on first write. Set regardless of whether the plugin is on raw `$PATH` or in the managed dir, so plugins get the same contract either way. Omitted only in degenerate environments where the per-user data root cannot be resolved (e.g. no home dir, no `LOCALAPPDATA`/`XDG_DATA_HOME`/`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`); the parent CLI prints a warning to stderr in that case.

The working directory is not changed — external commands run in the user's current directory, the same as any other shell command.

### Environment filtering

Unlike `kubectl` and `gh`, which forward the parent's full environment to every plugin, Entire filters the parent environment through a small allowlist before invoking an external command. ## What External Commands Do Not Get

  * No checkpoint integration. File modifications are not tracked in checkpoints. External commands do not appear in `entire activity`. If a tool needs to participate in the session/checkpoint lifecycle, it must use the agent protocol instead.
  * No transcript recording. External-command stdio is not captured.
  * No hook installation. External commands cannot register git hooks or agent hooks via the resolver. They are free to install their own, but `entire` does not coordinate.
  * No automatic update checks for the command itself. The CLI runs `versioncheck.CheckAndNotify` for the parent CLI's version, not the child's. Authors should handle their own update notifications.

## Telemetry

External-command invocations are tracked only for names on a hardcoded allowlist (`officialPlugins` in `cmd/entire/cli/plugin_official.go`). Third-party command names are never sent — even with telemetry opted in. The reasoning matches gh's extension-telemetry posture: arbitrary command names can carry sensitive identifiers (project names, vendor names), and the safest default is silence.

When an allowlisted command runs successfully, the CLI emits a `cli_plugin_executed` event with:

  * `plugin` — the command name
  * `command` — `entire <name>`
  * `cli_version`, `os`, `arch`, `isEntireEnabled`

Args and flags are deliberately not recorded.

Telemetry fires only when:

  1. The command name is in `officialPlugins`.
  2. `entire` settings have `Telemetry: true`.
  3. `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` is unset.
  4. The command exited with status 0. Failed/crashing invocations are not tracked, matching Cobra's `PersistentPostRun` semantics for built-in commands.

## Adding an Entire-Shipped Command to the Allowlist

When publishing an Entire-owned external command (e.g. `entire-pgr`):

  1. Append the command name to `officialPlugins` in `cmd/entire/cli/plugin_official.go`.
  2. Match must be exact and case-sensitive — the binary on disk is `entire-<name>`.
  3. Update or add tests if the command has unusual telemetry shape.

Once allowlisted, `cli_plugin_executed` events for that command will flow through the existing PostHog pipeline.

## Comparison with the Agent Protocol

 | External Commands  | Agent Protocol
--- | --- | ---
Binary name pattern  | `entire-<name>`  | `entire-agent-<name>`
Discovery  | Lazy, on first non-built-in arg  | Lazy at command entry, gated by the `external_agents` setting, which is honored only from an untracked `.entire/settings.local.json` (setup flows bypass the gate via `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` / `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways`)
Communication  | Process exec; stdio passthrough  | Subcommand protocol; JSON over stdin/stdout
Versioning  | None  | `ENTIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` envelope
Lifecycle integration  | None  | Full (sessions, checkpoints, hooks, transcripts)
Telemetry  | Allowlist only  | Standard agent telemetry
Working directory  | User's cwd  | Repository root
Use when  | You want to add a CLI verb  | You want an AI agent to participate in checkpointed sessions

Manages telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy options, and summary
provider configuration. Agent installation is handled by 'entire agent'.

Examples:
  entire configure                                # Show this help
  entire configure --telemetry=false              # Opt out of telemetry
  entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path       # Reinstall git hook with absolute path
  entire configure --force                        # Reinstall git hook
  entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:org/checkpoints   # or gitlab:org/checkpoints
  entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs      # Move a legacy repo to per-checkpoint git refs
  entire configure --checkpoint-push-policy manual   # Keep checkpoints local until 'entire checkpoint push'
  entire configure --summarize-provider claude-code
  entire configure --summarize-timeout-seconds 300   # 5m deadline for explain --generate

Usage:
  entire configure [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path          Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --checkpoint-backend string       Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-policy string   When checkpoints upload for this clone: automatic (on git push) or manual (only with 'entire checkpoint push'). Applies to the whole clone; --local and --project don't change where it is saved
      --checkpoint-remote string        Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                           Reinstall the Entire git hook
  -h, --help                            help for configure
      --local                           Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --project                         Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --skip-push-sessions              Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --summarize-model string          Set the model hint used by explain --generate
      --summarize-provider string       Set the provider used by explain --generate (e.g., claude-code, codex, antigravity, pi, opencode, cursor, copilot-cli)
      --summarize-timeout-seconds int   Set the hard deadline (seconds) for explain --generate summary generation. 0 clears the setting, leaving summary generation unbounded.
      --telemetry                       Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

# Sessions and Checkpoints

## Overview

Entire CLI creates checkpoints for AI coding sessions. The system is agent-agnostic - it works with Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, or any tool that triggers Entire hooks.

This document covers the domain model shared by both checkpoint storage backends. For how the git-refs backend stores checkpoints as one ref per checkpoint — its layout, push/fetch model, read routing, and configuration — see Ref-Based Checkpoint Backend.

### Session

A Session is a unit of work: one agent conversation, from its first hook to session end. Its live state is `session.State` (`session/state.go`), persisted per session at `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` and shared across worktrees:
    
    type State struct {
        SessionID        string          // agent-provided session identifier
        BaseCommit       string          // commit the pending work sits on; moves with HEAD
        WorktreeID       string          // internal git worktree name; empty for the main worktree
### Committed Checkpoints

Branch: `entire/checkpoints/v1`

Committed checkpoints sync to exactly one git remote — the elected checkpoint sync remote, resolved in this order:

  1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` if set — fail-closed when it names a remote that is not configured (checkpoint sync is disabled until fixed, since this is explicit user intent).
  2. The captured election, if its remote is still configured — fail-soft otherwise (capture is automatic state, so a renamed/removed remote falls through instead of disabling sync).
  3. `origin`, if configured.
  4. The sole configured remote.
  5. The first remote in `.git/config` order.

Capture is how the election follows the user's actual push habit with zero configuration: during pre-push, when the push target agrees with the branch's declared push destination (`branch.<name>.pushRemote` → `remote.pushDefault` → `branch.<name>.remote` — the config a bare `git push` resolves through) and differs from the current election, that remote is persisted as the captured election (git common dir, `entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json`, list-shaped for the future multi-remote set), a one-line stderr notice announces the change, and the same push carries the checkpoints.   * On the git-branch primary, a delete must not leave a v1 push destination holding the copy. The local removal is a `v1` commit, and the next pre-push fast-forwards every destination (each pushurl of the sync remote, or the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL derived from any remote) to it, deleting those copies too. `--local-only` probes only those destinations; a delete whose selection leaves one out is refused before anything is written when that destination holds a `v1` copy (remedy: also delete there, or use the git-refs backend) or cannot be reached (remedy: retry once reachable). Known limitations: a push to a not-yet-elected remote can elect it on the spot (capture) and send `v1` there; such a remote is not checked. A dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL derived from a remote spelling this clone cannot authenticate to probes as unreachable, so the refusal ("retry when reachable") persists until that spelling works. With `push_sessions` disabled nothing is pushed, but re-enabling it later carries the removal to the sync remote.
  * a logs-only resume point — a commit on the current branch whose `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer resolves to a checkpoint that is already condensed onto `entire/checkpoints/v1`, listed so its session transcript can be restored from there (file state would need a git checkout).

"Pending" describes the listing, not a guarantee that the work behind every row is un-condensed: `ListLogsOnlyPendingCheckpoints` builds the second kind by scanning branch history against committed checkpoint storage.

Either shape can be listed, but the CLI cannot restore working files to it: the file-restoring path (`Rewind`, `PreviewRewind`, `CanRewind`) was removed along with the `rewind` commands. `RestoreLogsOnly` still writes a checkpoint's session logs into the agent's session directory for `entire resume`, and leaves the worktree alone.

## Concurrent Sessions

Multiple AI sessions can run concurrently on the same base commit:

  1. Notice on start - When a session starts while other sessions in the same worktree have pending steps or task content on the same base commit (`CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints`), an informational message is shown
  2. Both proceed - Each session keeps its own state file, touched files, and metadata directory
  3. Condensation - On commit, every session whose touched files overlap the commit is condensed into the same checkpoint, each in its own numbered subfolder

Default brain artifacts are local and inspectable. Deterministic refresh, semantic indexing, and local history indexing do not require a hosted model.

### Brain without fact extraction

Extracting facts uses an available agent CLI and can send session content to its model provider and incur token charges. Without an agent CLI, this step is skipped.

To build without fact extraction or a background service, use:
    
    entire brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon

Configured remote history sources and hosted memories sync also use the network; see privacy and egress for controls.

### Background maintenance and memory sync

The watcher updates local repository context and runs distillation within the configured budget. For connected repositories, Brain syncs after a post-commit checkpoint notification and after distillation saves its results. Existing push notifications and manual sync remain supported. The watcher does not upload or pull memories on idle ticks. Brain no longer processes session-end notifications.

Sync sends new or changed record versions and saves server acknowledgements locally. Overlapping uploads use one process lock; successful batches do not need another upload. Failed or interrupted uploads remain eligible for the next sync event. Original session, checkpoint, and commit references remain unchanged.

## Activate it for your agent

For Claude capture, follow the [capture requirements](docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md#claude-capture-requirement).

Brain is set up per [repository](docs/reference.md#3a-what-setup-needs-first-and-what-it-does-not). Start in a local Git repository with at least one commit:

```sh
entire brain setup
```

By default, `setup` indexes the repository, extracts facts from up to 25 past sessions in the background, installs a watcher to keep the memory updated, and installs the agent instructions. The watcher runs as a persistent service on macOS and Linux with systemd.

The agent instructions live in these files, created or updated by `setup`:

- `.entire/agent-guide.md`: the agent instructions. Rerunning setup replaces this file.
- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`: references to the guide inside managed blocks. Your text outside those blocks is preserved.

The guide is assembled from whichever products have been **activated**, and each
product activates itself. `entire brain setup` on its own writes a
Brain-only guide containing no Graph instructions at all — installing Graph does
not change that, because activation is recorded in the guide rather than probed.
Run `entire graph setup` too if you want both.

The two setups compose in **either order**. The guide text is mirrored between
the two products, so both render the same combined guide; each run only adds its
own product to the recorded activation.

Review the generated files and commit them together when the instructions should apply to your team. Restart your agent or reload its repository instructions so it picks up the guide.

See the [agent integration guide](docs/reference.md#how-agents-use-the-brain) and [coordination contract](docs/agent-coordination.md) for more setup details.

### Brain without fact extraction

Extracting facts uses an available agent CLI and can send session content to its model provider and incur token charges. Without an agent CLI, this step is skipped. 

To build without fact extraction or a background service, use:

```sh
entire brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon
```

Configured remote history sources and hosted memories sync also use the network; see [privacy and egress](docs/reference.md#privacy-and-egress) for controls.

### Background maintenance and memory sync

The watcher updates local repository context and runs distillation within the configured budget.
For connected repositories, Brain syncs after a post-commit checkpoint notification and after distillation saves its results.
Existing push notifications and manual sync remain supported.
The watcher does not upload or pull memories on idle ticks.
Brain no longer processes session-end notifications.

Sync sends new or changed record versions and saves server acknowledgements locally.
Overlapping uploads use one process lock; successful batches do not need another upload.
Failed or interrupted uploads remain eligible for the next sync event.

Scan for session issues and offer to fix them.

Checks performed:
  1. Per-user config: report an invalid config.json, which makes most
     commands refuse to run. Doctor exits non-zero until it is fixed or
     removed.

  2. Disconnected metadata branches: detects when local and remote
     entire/checkpoints/v1 branches share no common ancestor (caused by a
     previous bug). Fixes by cherry-picking local checkpoints onto remote tip.

  3. Operational logs: warn when .entire/logs cannot be written. Every other
     diagnostic is delivered by writing there, and that write is silent about
     its own failure, so an unwritable log directory looks exactly like a repo
     where nothing ran.

  When Codex hooks are installed:
  4. Codex hook trust: warn when hooks declared in .codex/hooks.json
     lack a trusted_hash entry in the user's Codex config (i.e. /hooks
     review hasn't run yet on this machine, or a newer entire release
     added a hook the user hasn't approved yet).

  For each installed agent that reports hook-config drift:
  5. Hook config: warn when the installed hooks no longer match what this
     CLI writes (e.g. an older release wrote Claude Code tool matchers that
     no longer fire, or a committed Pi/OpenCode extension has gone stale).
     Fix by running 'entire agent add <agent>' (add --force if that does
     not fix it).

  6. Retired Gemini CLI hooks: remove Entire hook entries left in
     .gemini/settings.json. Gemini CLI support was removed; the entries now do
     nothing but run a no-op on every Gemini event.

  7. Summary provider: warn when summary_generation.provider names a registered
     agent that cannot generate text (e.g. factoryai-droid), which makes
     'entire checkpoint explain --generate' and 'entire dispatch' fail. Reports the file to change; does not rewrite it.

  8. Legacy shadow branches: report entire/<commit>-<worktree> branches older
     versions wrote at every turn. They hold full snapshots of the working
     tree and nothing reads them anymore. Fix with 'entire doctor --force',
     which deletes only the branches; a later 'git gc' frees the space once
     the unreachable objects are two weeks old ('git gc --prune=now' frees it
     at once but drops every unreachable object, so run it only when no other
     git process is active); a branch
     checked out in a worktree is left alone. Bare entire/<commit> branches
     are only pointed at ('entire clean --all --dry-run'), never deleted.

  9. Stuck sessions: sessions stuck in ACTIVE or ENDED phase that need cleanup.

A session is considered stuck if:
  - It is in ACTIVE phase with no interaction for over 1 hour
  - It is in ENDED phase with uncondensed checkpoint data

For each stuck session, you can choose to:
  - Condense: Save session data to permanent storage
  - Discard: Remove the session state
  - Skip: Leave the session as-is

Use --force to condense all fixable sessions without prompting.  Sessions that can't
be condensed will be discarded.

Without a terminal to prompt on (agents, CI), doctor reports each issue and

```

| phase | blocking? | spends tokens? | installed by default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. **instant core** — sessions, semantic index, seed, docs, history, entities | yes, seconds | **no**, deterministic | — |
| 2. **fact backfill** — distill past sessions into durable facts, newest first | no, detached | **yes** | yes, unless `--no-backfill` |
| 3. **watcher daemon** — a launchd agent / systemd user unit that keeps every set-up repo fresh | no | **yes**, per window | **yes, with no prompt**, unless `--no-daemon` |

Read the three rows as three separate consents, because `setup` asks for none of
them:

- **The instant core is free and deterministic.** No hosted-model call, no
  token. When it returns — seconds on a small repo, about a minute on a large
  one — the brain is queryable.
- **The backfill SPENDS TOKENS.** It distills your past sessions with an agent
  CLI, detached, newest first, capped at **25 sessions per pass**
  (`--backfill-budget`; `--backfill-budget 0` explicitly means the whole corpus
  in one spend). `--no-backfill` skips it entirely. It is also skipped on its
  own when no agent CLI is available.
- **The watcher is installed as a persistent background service, by default,
  without asking.** On macOS that is a launchd agent with `RunAtLoad` and
  `KeepAlive` registered through `launchctl bootstrap`; on Linux a systemd user unit
  with `Restart=always`, enabled with `systemctl --user enable --now`. It
  survives logout and reboot, and its gated distill step calls an agent, so it
  is a **recurring** spend, not a one-off. There is no confirmation prompt
  anywhere in `setup`. What there is, is a pre-flight line — the FIRST thing a
  run that will register a watcher prints, before any work, naming the label,
  the unit path, and both ways out:

  ```
  setup: background watcher: this run will install io.entire.brain-watch.<id> at
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.entire.brain-watch.<id>.plist — a persistent launchd
  service that starts again at every login; pass --no-daemon to skip it, or
  remove it later with `entire brain setup --uninstall-daemon`
  ```

  A re-run that finds the watcher already there says it *keeps* it rather than
  claiming a second install, and `--no-daemon` says nothing about a service it
  will not install. Pass `--no-daemon` if you do not want it, and
  `entire brain setup --uninstall-daemon` to stop and remove one you already
  have.

**So a default `setup` spends money, and then keeps spending.** It is not a
one-off build: it installs a background service whose gated step calls an agent.
Four gates bound it, and none of them is a quota you have to remember:

- `--backfill-budget` caps the background pass. It defaults to **25 sessions**,
  newest first — the newest sessions carry the facts you actually want. Setup
  prints what the cap did.
- `--distill-every` (default 24h) plus each repo's persisted watch cursor allow
  **one** gated agent run per repo per window, and survive restarts. That bounds
  how *often* the daemon spends; `--backfill-budget` bounds how *much* each
  spend costs — setup installs the watcher with the same per-pass session cap it
  gave the backfill, so a window can never quietly distill the whole remaining
  corpus.
- The distill cache reuses unchanged sessions unless forced, across every entry

Installed plugin "brain" → /Users/hedde/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-brain
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (code index, sessions,
               repository context, docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO
               agent tokens. The brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. Background distillation has a
recurring cost, bounded by five gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends
(default no, and a run with no terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is QUERYABLE, and queryable means
it can answer: at least one of the code index, the repository context or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire brain query", "entire brain brief" and
"entire brain overview" read, so "entire brain setup && entire brain query ..." cannot proceed on a
brain that has nothing to answer from. A component that fails without costing
that (a doc index, an entity index, a stale code index beside repository context
that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the
backfill, the workspace registration and the daemon install all still run;
"entire brain status" then shows that component as failed and "entire brain doctor" prints
the reason. setup exits non-zero when nothing usable exists: the brain
directory cannot be built, every component failed, the worktree is too dirty to
index, or the repository has no commits yet.

Re-running setup is safe: it detects the existing workspace membership and
daemon instead of duplicating them, resumes rather than restarts a backfill
that is still running, and keeps whatever --interval/--distill-every/--model/
--effort the previous run was given unless you pass the flag again.

Usage:
  entire-brain setup [path] [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string             Agent for the background backfill: auto, none, codex, claude-code (default "auto")
      --agent-hooks              Merge the Claude Code PreToolUse entry even if a previous run declined it
      --backfill                 Start the background fact backfill even if a previous run declined it (SPENDS TOKENS)
      --backfill-budget int      Cap sessions the background backfill distills in one pass, newest first (0 = explicitly unlimited: the WHOLE corpus in one spend) (default 25)
      --daemon                   Install the background watcher even if a previous run declined it
      --distill-every duration   Minimum interval between the daemon's gated agent runs (default 24h0m0s)
      --effort string            Reasoning effort for the background backfill (default "low")
  -h, --help                     help for setup
      --interval duration        Daemon poll interval (default 5m0s)
      --json                     Emit the setup report as JSON
      --model string             Cheap/fast model for the background backfill (recommended)
      --no-agent-hooks           Write the agent guide but do not merge the Claude Code PreToolUse entry (remembered)
      --no-backfill              Do not start the background fact backfill, which SPENDS TOKENS (remembered: later bare re-runs keep declining)
      --no-daemon                Run the instant phase and backfill but do not install the background watcher (remembered: later bare re-runs keep declining)
      --normal                   Reset the agent guide to normal guidance
      --strict                   Save strict (mandatory tool-use) guidance into the agent guide
      --uninstall-daemon         Stop and remove the background watcher, then exit
      --verbose                  Report every phase, component and path instead of the short summary
      --workspace string         Workspace the repo joins (created when absent) (default "default")
      --yes                      Answer the fact-backfill consent prompt with yes. Without it, a run with no terminal spends nothing
connect binds this repository to its hosted brain: it records the repo id and
API base URL (non-secrets only — the host CLI's own login mints a fresh token
per sync), then runs one immediate sync so the first pull happens right away.

Running connect (or the onboarding flow) is the ONLY way a repository starts
syncing: by default memories stay local and background triggers never connect
a repo on their own. Placement resolves through the host CLI (entire repo
view); pass --repo-id and --api-url to bypass resolution — a non-default cell
or a staging target. Re-running connect re-joins after 'entire brain
disconnect'.

Usage:
  entire-brain connect [flags]

Flags:
      --api-url string   Entire API base URL, https://
  -h, --help             help for connect
      --repo-id string   Hosted repo id (region-local ULID)
sync exchanges this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
over the per-fact wire: push this branch's memories, pull the team's delta feed.
It is the same exchange the background sync runs, except failures fail the
command instead of degrading silently.

Memory sync is hosted-only. The default target is the connected binding
('entire brain connect'); on an unconnected repo a plain sync fails and
memories stay local. The local-gitmeta backend was removed (COR-2236):
--memories-backend accepts only "http", and the explicit target resolves
flag > env > connected binding (--api-url/ENTIRE_API_URL,
--repo-id/ENTIRE_REPO_ID, --token/ENTIRE_API_TOKEN; on a connected repo the
binding supplies the target and the token is minted automatically).

ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS (or its deprecated alias ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY)
suppresses all hosted sync regardless of defaults and flags.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories sync [flags]

Flags:
      --api-url string            Entire API base URL, https:// (overrides ENTIRE_API_URL)
      --branch string             Branch to sync (default: current branch)
  -h, --help                      help for sync
      --json                      Emit the sync result as JSON
      --memories-backend string   Memory-set backend; only "http" (the hosted per-fact wire) is supported
      --repo-id string            Target repo id (overrides ENTIRE_REPO_ID)
      --token string              Entire API bearer token (overrides ENTIRE_API_TOKEN)
