+Entire Trails use the existing GitHub mirror. Entire recording is enabled for
+Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity through generated lifecycle hooks; current
+Entire no longer supports Gemini CLI capture. Gemini still follows the shared
+Trail instructions. Brain supplies repository memory and hosted synchronization;
+read the setup and validation requirements in the workflow guide.
+Keep authentication, personal settings and session caches local. The migration
*** Update File: /Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/594b/evorto/.agents/entire-workflow.md
@@
-Optional Entire session/checkpoint capture is independent of Trails. Do not
-restore old hooks merely to use hosting or code review. If recording is adopted
-later, verify supported agents against the installed CLI and review where
-checkpoint data is uploaded, especially for this public repository. Do not
-commit credentials or transcript caches.
+### Recording and shared memory
+
+Lukas explicitly enabled recording and memory synchronization on 8 November
+2026. Use the generated Entire hooks for Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity.
+Entire CLI 0.13.1 rejects Gemini CLI capture as unsupported; do not restore the
+old no-op Gemini hooks. Gemini can use the shared instructions and Brain
+commands, and Antigravity is the supported Google recording integration.
+
+For a new clone, install Entire, authenticate with your own identity, then run:
+
+```sh
+entire enable --agent codex --project --telemetry=false --no-init-repo
+entire agent add claude-code
+entire agent add antigravity
+entire doctor
+entire plugin install brain
+entire brain setup --yes --backfill-budget 5
+entire brain connect
+entire brain memories sync --json
+entire brain status --json
+```
+
+Agent installation regenerates portable configuration; inspect the diff before
+committing updates. Git hooks and Brain services require per-machine setup;
+checking out tracked files alone does not install them. Keep telemetry off.
+Codex may discover `.codex/hooks.json` in the primary checkout instead of a
+linked worktree; follow `entire doctor`'s discovered path. Review the generated
+hooks through Codex `/hooks`, then restart/reload the agent. Do not synthesize
+trust records. Workspace trust and agent authentication stay per-user.
+
+The shared checkpoint backend is `git-refs`. Checkpoints upload with Git pushes
+to the configured sync remote, currently `origin`. Transcripts include prompts,
+responses and tool activity. This repository is public, so uploaded checkpoints
+are public; automatic redaction is best effort. Inspect sensitive sessions before
+publishing. Keep credentials, caches and `.entire/settings.local.json` untracked.
+Do not import unrelated project or machine-wide agent memory.
+
+Brain's generated `.entire/agent-guide.md` provides agent query/recall guidance.
+`setup` installs repository context and a background watcher; `connect` opts this
+repository into hosted team memory sync. The watcher uses a five-session cap per
+extraction pass and the default 24-hour extraction interval. Extraction calls an
+agent and consumes usage; deterministic indexes and memory transport are separate
+from that model work. Inspect `entire brain status` for real component readiness,
+backfill progress and daemon health. A successful connection with zero facts
+proves transport, not that useful memories have already been extracted.
+
+For deterministic symbol relationships and semantic context, use the official

Build/warm a committed-tree cache variant for matching queries

Usage:
  entire graph index --repo . [--head] [--force] [--profile syntax-only|fast|full] [--cache-dir path] [--report GRAPH_REPORT.md] [--format text|json|auto]

Prebuilds a durable, complete committed-tree snapshot. Later --head searches/neighbors can reuse it when caching is enabled and they resolve the same cache directory, profile, and ordered ignore/include inputs, with unchanged input-file contents and .graphignore. index defaults to full while query defaults to fast, so a default index does not warm a default query --head. Re-running index refreshes that cache variant: an unchanged tree hits, while a changed tree rebuilds. Pass --force to rebuild and overwrite the entry even when the tree is unchanged.

At a terminal it draws a live progress bar on stderr (only when it actually builds — a cache hit returns instantly) and prints a readable summary; piped or with --format json it emits the schema-versioned JSON summary that agents and CI consume. --report writes a human-readable GRAPH_REPORT.md rendered from the snapshot, so the same tree always renders the same bytes. The cache defaults to the platform per-user cache dir (macOS ~/Library/Caches/entire-graph; XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache elsewhere); --cache-dir and ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR override it.

A repo-root .graphignore (gitignore syntax) is honored by every graph command, on top of .gitignore. Use it for tracked-but-vendored/generated sources — e.g. tree-sitter parser.c blobs — that otherwise surface as E_FILE_TOO_LARGE/E_PARSE_ERROR partial failures and a "degraded" completeness. Oversized/minified skips also no longer count toward "degraded" on their own.

Flags:
  --repo <path>             Repository to index (default: current repo)
  --head                    Accepted for symmetry with the query commands; index is always HEAD-only, so this is a no-op
  --force                   Rebuild from scratch and overwrite the cache even if the tree is unchanged
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; full favors call-graph correctness (default: full)
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --report <path>           Also write a human-readable GRAPH_REPORT.md
  --format text|json|auto   Summary format; auto = text at a terminal, json when piped (default: auto)
  --ignore-file <path>      Extra gitignore-style rules to exclude paths (repeatable)
  --include-file <path>     Re-include ignored paths (gitignore-style; not an allowlist, repeatable)

Examples:
  entire graph index --repo . --head
  entire graph index --repo . --head --format json

Aliases:
  memories, facts

Available Commands:
  files        Write durable memories out as plain Markdown files you can grep, read and diff
  gc           Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  global       List memories recorded globally rather than for one repository
  import       Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  map          Render the synthesized memory outline (summaries + structure) with progressive disclosure
  outline      Generate the synthesized hierarchical memory outline (agent rollup summaries)
  retract      Mark a memory as retracted (no longer true); pruned later by gc
  status       Summarize durable memory readiness without refreshing or writing
  storage      Inspect or migrate memory storage
  sync         Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
  tree         Show memories as a navigable hierarchy with progressive disclosure
  vitality     Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for memories

Use "entire-brain memories [command] --help" for more information about a command.
Search the brain (BM25 lexical ranking). Supply the text positionally or with --query. Flags may appear before or after the text.

Usage:
  entire-brain query [query] [flags]

Flags:
      --after string               Conversation source only: sessions at or after this time (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD)
      --agent string               Conversation source only: exchanges captured by this agent/harness (e.g. "Claude Code", "Codex")
      --before string              Conversation source only: sessions before this time (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD)
      --branch string              Branch for memories (default: current); with --source conversation also filters exchanges to that captured branch
      --concept stringArray        Conversation source only: additional concept (repeatable, up to 4); sessions must match the query AND every concept
      --format string              Output format: json or cli (QMD-style alias for --json)
  -h, --help                       help for query
      --include-abstract           Conversation source only: include bounded evidence-linked session previews (never affects ranking)
      --json                       Emit machine-readable JSON
      --keyword                    Match keywords and identifiers only
      --limit int                  Maximum results (default 10)
      --no-global                  Exclude global memories from this request
  -n, --number int                 Maximum results (QMD-style alias for --limit) (default 10)
      --patterns                   Also surface relevant pattern:/theme: pointers (does not change facts/history/docs ranking)
      --query string               Query text (alternative to the positional query)
      --recency                    Prefer recent dated results (not supported for source conversation)
      --recency-half-life string   Recency half-life as a positive Go duration, e.g. 720h (default 2160h; requires --recency)
      --semantic                   Compatibility alias: semantic retrieval was removed; ranking is BM25 lexical
      --session string             Conversation source only: exchanges from this session id (also disables the per-session diversity cap)
      --source string              Restrict retrieval to one source: all, fact, history, conversation, or doc (default all; conversation is experimental opt-in)
capabilities requires --json

item.aggregated_output:
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, repository
context, docs, history, code-index records, and durable memories, then exposes
retrieval, verification, and evaluation surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup              Build the brain and start background updates
  add                Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  agent-guide        Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  webhook            Notify another service when this brain changes
  config             Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview           Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief              Gather relevant context for a task
  query              Search the brain (BM25 lexical ranking)
  get                Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get          Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash               Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable memories & patterns:
  recall             Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch
  remember           Record a durable memory about this repository
  distill            Extract durable memories from sessions (requires an agent)
  memories           Inspect, retract, and garbage-collect durable memories
  connect            Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  disconnect         Stop syncing this repository with its hosted brain
  verify             Verify durable memory anchors against local retained sources
  patterns           Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code index & context:
  inspect            Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show               Show one code-index record
  viz                Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

Brain state & maintenance:
  status             Show brain coverage, freshness, and workspace state
  stats              Show brain record counts and breakdowns

Workspaces & sharing:
  workspace          Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces
  bundle             Import or export local brain bundles

Troubleshooting & operations:
  memories import    Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  memories sync      Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
  memories gc        Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  memories vitality  Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)
  memory             Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  entities           Find checkpoints and sessions that changed a symbol
  repair             Rebuild Graph's committed-tree code index
  docs               Inspect how non-code documents are read into the brain
  refresh            Create or refresh the repository brain
  watch              Keep the brain up to date automatically
  stop               Pause background brain work on this machine
  start              Resume background brain work paused by `stop`
  reset              Remove local generated brain data
  repo-identity      Find and resolve conflicting brain stores

Miscellaneous:
  path               Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  capabilities       List supported features and retrieval sources
  doctor             Diagnose environment and brain pipeline problems
  version            Print plugin version
  help               Help about any command

Flags:
  -h, --help       help for entire-brain
      --help-all   List all commands, including hidden commands
  -v, --version    version for entire-brain

Use "entire-brain [command] --help" for more information about a command.

entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, repository
context, docs, history, code-index records, and durable memories, then exposes
retrieval, verification, and evaluation surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup              Build the brain and start background updates
  add                Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  agent-guide        Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  webhook            Notify another service when this brain changes
  config             Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview           Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief              Gather relevant context for a task
  query              Search the brain (BM25 lexical ranking)
  get                Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get          Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash               Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable memories & patterns:
  recall             Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch
  remember           Record a durable memory about this repository
  distill            Extract durable memories from sessions (requires an agent)
  memories           Inspect, retract, and garbage-collect durable memories
  connect            Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  disconnect         Stop syncing this repository with its hosted brain
  verify             Verify durable memory anchors against local retained sources
  patterns           Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code index & context:
  inspect            Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show               Show one code-index record
  viz                Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

Brain state & maintenance:
  status             Show brain coverage, freshness, and workspace state
  stats              Show brain record counts and breakdowns

Workspaces & sharing:
  workspace          Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces
  bundle             Import or export local brain bundles

Troubleshooting & operations:
  memories import    Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  memories sync      Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
  memories gc        Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  memories vitality  Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)
  memory             Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  entities           Find checkpoints and sessions that changed a symbol
  repair             Rebuild Graph's committed-tree code index
  docs               Inspect how non-code documents are read into the brain
  refresh            Create or refresh the repository brain
  watch              Keep the brain up to date automatically
  stop               Pause background brain work on this machine
  start              Resume background brain work paused by `stop`
  reset              Remove local generated brain data
  repo-identity      Find and resolve conflicting brain stores

Miscellaneous:
  path               Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  capabilities       List supported features and retrieval sources
  doctor             Diagnose environment and brain pipeline problems
  version            Print plugin version
  help               Help about any command

  -v, --version    version for entire-brain

## Continuous memory added to scope

Lukas explicitly welcomes Entire memory sync and wants its recommended useful native workflow. Install/configure the official Brain plugin and shared agent guidance, connect repository-scoped hosted memory where supported, and verify actual sync status. Keep global Codex/user memory outside this project migration. Installed Entire CLI 0.13.1 explicitly rejects Gemini CLI as no longer supported; use Antigravity as the supported Google recording integration while retaining Gemini workflow instructions. Generated Codex hooks resolve through the primary checkout and need verification there; do not claim the active worktree records merely because it contains a hooks file.

## Recording decision confirmed — 8 November 2026

Lukas confirmed Gemini CLI and Google Antigravity, and explicitly requested restoring Entire session recording, including prompts and tool activity. This supersedes the pending/workflow-only assumption. Codex owns extending local child branch codex/<issue id="66c4077f-4104-439f-97bf-5a57f6a7dc79" label="EVO-54" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-54/migrate-git-hosting-and-protected-review-to-entire" />-entire-workflow with current supported recording integrations for Codex, Claude, Gemini CLI and Antigravity, portable shared settings, and updated onboarding/recording instructions. Use installed CLI/generated upstream integration formats; preserve unrelated settings and keep caches/credentials untracked. Verify hook installation and settings before claiming recording readiness; distinguish generated/configuration checks from observed agent-session capture. No automatic invitations, access removal, paid-plan cancellation or deployment is part of this configuration slice.

## Local implementation prepared — 8 November 2026

Intent-only migration Trail: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/3](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/3>) . Local commit `75e227d1f57b72c96cadd8e07a45b6254896e822` on `codex/evo-54-entire-workflow`, based on PR209 head `6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd`. Six Markdown files: shared Entire policy in AGENTS.md, Claude/Gemini entrypoints, updated agent README, detailed `.agents/entire-workflow.md` migration checklist, and Knope change file. Codex and Antigravity use AGENTS.md; Gemini/Claude import it. No session hooks restored. Treat Antimatter as Antigravity based on existing local worktree; explicit clarification and optional recording preference remain pending.

Validation: lint passed with three existing warnings; format:write and focused Prettier check passed; Knope 0.23.0 --validate passed; import/path/change-file assertions and git diff --check passed. Clean local working tree after commit. No application behavior changed. Full publication-equivalent runtime/security/browser gate has NOT run for this new child; no push or PR creation. Complete that gate before linking/publishing the code branch (Trail 3 currently has intent only). Git Town created the branch; its later sync/setup required a TTY because PR209 removes Git Town configuration, so no stack synchronization/publication was claimed.

Access/billing evidence: GitHub lists heddendorp (admin), FranzZehetleitner and laurenskuchta (write); Entire mirror grant listing returns only github:heddendorp. Verify each collaborator's own Entire login/access; absence alone does not establish the cause. GitHub org API reports enterprise plan, one filled seat, one public repository and zero private repositories. Actual invoice, enterprise relationship, renewal and downgrade effective date remain unverified. <issue id="57ccf8be-84d5-48db-9781-ea1183952dd2" label="EVO-57" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-57/cancel-the-paid-github-subscription-after-verified-cutover" /> now records paid-org cancellation while preserving the GitHub mirror and necessary upstream grants. No invitations, access removal, billing change, merge or deployment occurred.

## Expanded authorized scope — 8 November 2026

Lukas requested collaborator onboarding to Entire and shared repository instructions/configuration for Codex, Claude and Gemini/Antigravity (tool name clarification pending), with all workflow changes recorded. Codex will prepare a reviewable child change above PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> so the earlier cleanup cannot erase the new agent entrypoints. Shared AGENTS.md remains canonical; thin tool-specific entrypoints direct agents to the same Trail workflow. Do not re-enable optional transcript recording without resolving that separate choice. Verify against installed CLI and official tool instruction-loading documentation; run lint/format after edits and validate paths/config. Preserve application behavior and full publication gates.

Constraint discovered: installed CLI states that GitHub mirror repository access follows GitHub upstream and grants are read-only in Entire; moving collaborator daily work to Entire does not decouple repository authorization from GitHub. Record this explicitly, preserve current access until the replacement is verified, and use native hosting as a later distinct decision if independent Entire access is required. Do not remove collaborators from GitHub on the assumption that the mirror has independent grants.

## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly selected the existing GitHub mirror as the working flow, superseding the fresh-repository/new-initial-commit plan below. Use Entire Trails over `gh/evorto-app/app`; retain GitHub history, PRs and required checks during this phase. No repository recreation or ancestry reset is planned for this phase.

Codex in the current consolidation chat owns inventory and linking existing PR branches into Entire Trails. Initial inventory: PR208 Stripe webhook claim fencing and draft PR209 <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> tooling cleanup; no open Trails existed. Mirror is ready in EU and US. Preserve both independent changes, existing reviews and exact heads. Verify Trail/PR association and report merge gates before changing readiness or merging. Keep required review/CI protections; no forced merges, deployments or subscription changes. Broader RWX migration remains separate under <issue id="290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e" label="EVO-50" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test" />.

Acceptance for this phase: both existing branches are accessible through Trails, linked PRs/checks and remaining gates are recorded, and the mirror-based daily workflow is concrete. The earlier fresh-repository criteria below are historical and superseded where they conflict.

## Goal

Prepare Entire-native hosting and replace GitHub-specific review protections without losing recoverable work.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.
* Preserve the original repository, historical refs, pending local/remote work and agent history recoverably outside the new repository. Resolve or explicitly defer/carry/archive outstanding work before choosing the snapshot; do not lose work that has not reached main.
* Configure canonical remotes, access and review rules. Verify required approvals/checks and protections against bypass, accidental deletion and history rewriting.
* Install/connect RWX and verify commit/Trail checks and failure blocking. Audit integration limitations rather than assuming GitHub feature parity.
* Reconcile <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> cleanup and <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> publication guidance; configure only required Entire tooling and update local-agent instructions.
* Document how Linear issues link to Trails/branches and how release tooling will work. Do not assume native Linear status sync exists.
* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

## Execution

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

## Consolidation verified — 8 November 2026

Created Entire Trail 1 for PR208: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1>) and Trail 2 for PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" />: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2>) . `entire trail ci-pr` returned the existing PR numbers 208 and 209; no replacement PRs or code pushes were needed. Exact heads remain 914f2d9b2ca7d03a0445ba958550712d6afc853e and 6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd. Both show CI/gate success and clean conflicts. PR208 is one commit behind main; PR209 is up to date. Read-only merge dry runs say mergeable, but all four Entire gates (approvals, checks, findings, up_to_date) are disabled. Dry-run success is therefore not proof of equivalent GitHub protection or release readiness. No merge or readiness change performed.

Working flow: retain GitHub origin; create a Trail linked to a feature branch; use ci-pr to link/create its GitHub PR for checks; inspect Trail checks/findings and GitHub review requirements; merge only after required local verification and both platforms' applicable gates. Entire approvals and GitHub approvals are separate. Optional session recording is independent.

Open decisions: whether/how to migrate the Linear backlog into intent-only Trails (titles, bodies, owners, priorities and source links can be represented, but preserving dependency/status/comment history needs an explicit migration design); configure and validate Entire gates; reconcile checked-in agent workflow guidance through a separate reviewed change. Linear remains the canonical issue tracker under current repository policy until that policy is deliberately changed. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.

* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

## Current direction — 8 November 2026

Lukas explicitly selected the existing GitHub mirror as the working flow, superseding the fresh-repository/new-initial-commit plan below. Use Entire Trails over `gh/evorto-app/app`; retain GitHub history, PRs and required checks during this phase. No repository recreation or ancestry reset is planned for this phase.

Codex in the current consolidation chat owns inventory and linking existing PR branches into Entire Trails. Initial inventory: PR208 Stripe webhook claim fencing and draft PR209 <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> tooling cleanup; no open Trails existed. Mirror is ready in EU and US. Preserve both independent changes, existing reviews and exact heads. Verify Trail/PR association and report merge gates before changing readiness or merging. Keep required review/CI protections; no forced merges, deployments or subscription changes. Broader RWX migration remains separate under <issue id="290c0cf2-ab37-4821-8b0b-20872dc4685e" label="EVO-50" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test" />.

Acceptance for this phase: both existing branches are accessible through Trails, linked PRs/checks and remaining gates are recorded, and the mirror-based daily workflow is concrete. The earlier fresh-repository criteria below are historical and superseded where they conflict.

## Goal

Prepare Entire-native hosting and replace GitHub-specific review protections without losing recoverable work.

## Migration history decision

On 8 November 2026, Lukas clarified: “I want to only move one state of main with a new initial commit”.

Start the Entire repository from one verified snapshot of the finalized main branch, with a new initial commit and no imported Git ancestry. Record the original main commit SHA so the snapshot can be traced back to its source. Preserve the old repository and outstanding local/remote work recoverably; decide the disposition of unresolved PRs and branches before selecting the final snapshot. This supersedes the earlier history-import proposal and does not authorize merging or closing PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Create and verify one new initial commit from the agreed final main snapshot. Record the original main commit SHA and confirm the snapshot contents match; do not import old Git ancestry or historical branches/tags into the new repository by default.
* Preserve the original repository, historical refs, pending local/remote work and agent history recoverably outside the new repository. Resolve or explicitly defer/carry/archive outstanding work before choosing the snapshot; do not lose work that has not reached main.
* Configure canonical remotes, access and review rules. Verify required approvals/checks and protections against bypass, accidental deletion and history rewriting.
* Install/connect RWX and verify commit/Trail checks and failure blocking. Audit integration limitations rather than assuming GitHub feature parity.
* Reconcile <issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" /> cleanup and <issue id="781c49f9-e07b-45ba-998d-593fd5f1924c" label="EVO-9" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-9/require-prs-and-document-linear-linked-naming" /> publication guidance; configure only required Entire tooling and update local-agent instructions.
* Document how Linear issues link to Trails/branches and how release tooling will work. Do not assume native Linear status sync exists.
* Keep GitHub available during validation. Test recovery from an independent Git copy and document reverse migration.
* Final canonical-remote switch follows the cutover criteria in the validation subissue; preparing Entire is not permission to retire GitHub early.

## Execution

This issue records planned work. Updating the history strategy does not execute a migration, change remotes or settings, merge or close PRs, deploy, or cancel a subscription.

## Consolidation verified — 8 November 2026

Created Entire Trail 1 for PR208: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/1/changes/app/1>) and Trail 2 for PR209/<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude" />: [https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2](<https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/2/changes/app/2>) . `entire trail ci-pr` returned the existing PR numbers 208 and 209; no replacement PRs or code pushes were needed. Exact heads remain 914f2d9b2ca7d03a0445ba958550712d6afc853e and 6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd. Both show CI/gate success and clean conflicts. PR208 is one commit behind main; PR209 is up to date. Read-only merge dry runs say mergeable, but all four Entire gates (approvals, checks, findings, up_to_date) are disabled. Dry-run success is therefore not proof of equivalent GitHub protection or release readiness. No merge or readiness change performed.

Working flow: retain GitHub origin; create a Trail linked to a feature branch; use ci-pr to link/create its GitHub PR for checks; inspect Trail checks/findings and GitHub review requirements; merge only after required local verification and both platforms' applicable gates. Entire approvals and GitHub approvals are separate. Optional session recording is independent.

Open decisions: whether/how to migrate the Linear backlog into intent-only Trails (titles, bodies, owners, priorities and source links can be represented, but preserving dependency/status/comment history needs an explicit migration design); configure and validate Entire gates; reconcile checked-in agent workflow guidance through a separate reviewed change. issues.body:
## Purpose

Simplify Evorto's root tooling around Codex and Claude, matching the clarified EVO-8 scope. The earlier module-guidance rewrite is reverted from this PR.

Linear: https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/simplify-root-tooling-for-codex-and-claude

## Changes

- Remove the tracked Air, Gemini, Entire, JetBrains and VS Code config folders.
- Remove Entire session-recording lifecycle hooks, its Codex hook feature toggle, and the Copilot cloud-agent setup. Retain required Copilot code review and its source-only setup.
- Keep Codex MCP/worktree setup and shared skills, EditorConfig, Prettier and ESLint configuration. Add a small CLAUDE.md that imports the canonical AGENTS.md.
- Remove git-town.toml and the Git Town stack-display workflow. Replace mandatory Git Town commands with ordinary Git/GitHub PR guidance and optional GitHub-native stacked PRs.
- Ignore retired tool/editor directories so local settings do not return to source control. Add a Knope change file.

## Project-local cleanup

Entire's session-recording Git hooks and agent hooks/settings were removed from all seven existing Evorto worktrees. Hook/session metadata was archived recoverably outside the repository. Global tools/settings, other projects, historical commits/branch refs, and inactive historical Git Town branch metadata were preserved. Those local uninstall steps are not represented by the tracked diff; existing checkouts outside this machine should disable their own installed Entire hooks when adopting the change.

GitHub confirms native stacked PRs are generally available on all github.com plans: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-06-stacked-pull-requests-generally-available/ . The optional gh stack extension provides local stack automation; ordinary Git remains usable. No extension installation or protection-rule change is included here.

## Compatibility with the planned hosting move

The removal concerns optional session recording/checkpoints, not Entire Git hosting. Entire's documented repository workflow uses CLI/git-remote-entire, authentication and a native remote; `entire enable` adds session capture separately. Installed CLI/global settings are untouched. The planned hosting/RWX migration is tracked in [EVO-50](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-50/move-evorto-to-entire-and-rwx-with-smaller-workflows-and-reliable-test); it will create a new repository from one approved main snapshot with a new initial commit, while preserving existing history separately. This PR does not perform that migration, re-enable capture, switch remotes, or cancel GitHub. Current PR/Linear/Copilot and verification requirements remain in force until an authorized cutover.

Official references: [Entire repository guide](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository), [CLI recording setup](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md), [RWX integration](https://www.rwx.com/docs/getting-started/entire).

## Verification

Re-run for clarified head `6de30fa7a390ede188330deae00f2ad4920f32dd`.

- Frozen dependency installation, Knope, formatting, lint and diff checks passed. Lint reports three pre-existing warnings.
- Server unit tests: 2,692 passed. Application unit tests: 1,707 passed. PostgreSQL integration tests: 383 passed.
- Terraform validation and HIGH/CRITICAL config scan passed.
- Linux/amd64 image build, runtime/size/source-map checks, SBOM and HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability scan passed.
- Functional/documentation baseline: all 275 tests passed in 3.3 minutes; the isolated stack was removed and original local app restoration verified.
- Retained entrypoint/ignore checks and project-wide Entire-hook removal assertions passed. Independent read-only review found no actionable regression.

No application behavior, schema, deployment or UI changes. No direct-main push or merge. Copilot completed a fresh review of this exact head and recommended approval with no open issues.


## Review and hosted validation

- [Copilot review of 6de30fa7a39](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/209#pullrequestreview-5817220698): approval recommended, no actionable comments or unresolved threads. Copilot skipped the 18 deleted generated .idea files; those deletions and retained shared settings were checked locally.
- [PR Quality](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/actions/runs/42463471253): all required jobs and CI/gate passed on the same head. CodeQL and source-only Copilot setup also passed. Optional CodeRabbit skipped this draft.
- PR remains a draft and unmerged.

issues.body:
A Stripe webhook handler that runs longer than five minutes can lose its claim to a retry. Previously, its late failure deleted the retry's receipt, and its late success could mark that receipt processed while the retry was still running.

Give every receipt attempt a fresh PostgreSQL-generated UUID, including stale-claim takeovers. Completion and release now require the exact event, attempt token, and processing status. Keep payment transitions and their existing transactional guards unchanged.

Validation:

- Added three real PostgreSQL regressions for late failure, late success, and immediate release/replacement at an identical timestamp. All three fail with the former event-only mutation predicates and pass with the fix.
- Complete local browser/documentation baseline: 275 passed, zero skipped/retried.
- Complete local server suite: 2,692 passed.
- Complete local Angular suite: 1,707 passed.
- Complete local PostgreSQL suite: 386 passed, zero skipped.
- Lint passes with three existing warnings; formatting and Knope validation pass.
- Local infrastructure validation/security scan and Linux/amd64 runtime build, inspection, SBOM, and HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability scan pass.

Schema/runtime review: Evorto is not deployed, so no live-upgrade compatibility path is required. Adds non-null `stripe_webhook_events.claim_id` with a database UUID default. Verified the additive upgrade against synthetic pre-change processing and processed receipts: all existing fields and microsecond timestamps were preserved exactly, each existing row received a distinct token, and new receipts received their own default token. Real local data was untouched. Fencing protects receipt ownership, while business-side idempotency remains the responsibility of the existing payment transactions. Local tests use synthetic data, a separate disposable PostgreSQL 17 container, and Stripe mocks/test mode. No production data, credential changes, merge, or deployment.

Review the token renewal on takeover, both conditional terminal writes, and propagation of the owned token through the handler's normal and failure paths.

- `main` <!-- branch-stack -->
  - **fix: preserve recovered Stripe webhook claim ownership** :point\_left:

### 🟢 Approval recommended The webhook receipt ownership change has no active review issues. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR protects recovered Stripe webhook receipts from late completion or failure by an older handler, while leaving existing payment transaction guards unchanged. **Changes:** - Adds a database-generated claim UUID, renewed on each stale-claim takeover. - Requires the event ID, owned claim token, and processing status for completion and release. - Adds PostgreSQL regressions and updates unit-test expectations and architecture documentation. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​server/​http/​stripe-webhook.web-handler.ts` | Renews claim tokens and carries ownership through completion and failure paths. | | `src/​server/​http/​stripe-webhook.web-handler.spec.ts` | Verifies token-aware receipt SQL and parameters. | | `src/​server/​http/​stripe-webhook-claim.postgres.spec.ts` | Tests late outcomes and replacement claims at identical timestamps. | | `src/​db/​schema/​stripe-webhook-events.ts` | Adds non-null `claim_id` with a database UUID default. | | `ARCHITECTURE.md` | Documents receipt ownership protection and its boundaries. | | `.changeset/​webhook-claim-ownership.md` | Records the webhook ownership fix as a patch release. |
Review effort: Balanced

Thanks Lukas, this closes the B1 gap from the hackathon review cleanly. I walked the claim lifecycle at `914f2d9b` and found no blocker.

**Checked and agreed**
- Release and mark-processed now require `stripe_event_id + claim_id + status = 'processing'`, and takeover renews the token in SQL. So a late former owner can neither delete nor acknowledge a recovered claim, and a completed receipt can't be deleted, even by its own owner.
- Two concurrent takeovers can't both win: the conditional UPDATE re-checks `processed_at <= staleBefore` after the row lock, so the second one falls through to `duplicate-processing`.
- The handler carries the token it actually won (insert or takeover) into both the failure path and `finalizeClaim`.
- The three Postgres cases fail with main's event-only predicates (late failure, late success, same-timestamp replacement), so they prove the fence, including the status predicate.
- `uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` passes the expand policy, and the seeded e2e rows rely on the default.

**One change I'd suggest**
A lost fence is silent. `markWebhookEventProcessed` and `releaseWebhookEventClaim` drop the affected-row count, so a fenced-out owner returns its normal response and logs nothing. That's the moment worth seeing: a handler outlived the 5-minute lease while another worker ran the same side effects. Suggestion: return `'owned' | 'lost'` via `.returning(...)` and `logWarning` with `eventId`/`claimId` on `'lost'`, keeping the HTTP response as is. The Postgres spec could then assert `'lost'` directly, and a concurrent-takeover case would be a cheap extra.

**Two questions (pre-existing, fine outside this PR)**
1. After a lost receipt (crash between the business commit and mark-processed), an add-on Checkout replay hits `state-conflict` in `validateCheckoutSessionBinding` and returns 409, although `completePaidAddonPurchaseCheckout` handles `already_applied`. So the takeover replay releases, and Stripe retries until it gives up. I think `async_payment_failed` and add-on expiry behave the same way. Is that intended, or should these resolve to success like registration replays?
2. The insert stamps `processed_at` with DB `now()`, while takeover compares against app `new Date()`. Would a SQL-side cut-off (`now() - interval '5 minutes'`) be worth it, so the lease uses one clock?

Nit: the new ARCHITECTURE.md paragraph mixes the invariant with test-procedure notes. FYI, the title has no EVO id yet (new convention from EVO-9).

I didn't rerun the suites for this review; we ran the new Postgres spec 3/3 on this head during the hackathon review.

name: effect-ts
description: Use this skill whenever working in a repository that uses Effect, even if the current task is in a new file or the user does not explicitly ask for Effect help. Apply it to any work that should follow the repository's Effect patterns, conventions, architecture, or supporting tooling. Also use it for questions about Effect patterns, services, layers, schemas, streams, runtimes, or typed error handling.
---

# Effect Expert

Expert guidance for programming with the Effect library, covering error handling, dependency injection, composability, and testing patterns.

## Prerequisite

Before doing any other Effect-related work, check that `./repos/effect` exists at the root of the repository where the skill is being used.

If it does not exist, stop and prompt the user with the setup task documented in `./references/setup.md`.

## Research Strategy

Effect has many ways to accomplish the same task. Proactively research best practices when working with Effect patterns, especially for moderate to high complexity tasks.

Use the local guides in `./references/` first. They are the preferred source for best practices, conventions, and common implementation patterns.

Only go directly to the vendored Effect repo when:

- the guides do not cover the question
- you need exact API details or signatures
- you need deeper implementation details
- you need to verify a behavior against the source

### Research Sources

1. Local skill guides first. Start with the relevant files in `./references/` before doing deeper research.
2. Codebase patterns second. Examine similar patterns in the current project before implementing. If Effect patterns already exist, follow them for consistency. If no patterns exist, skip this step.
3. Effect source code last. For gaps in the guides, complex type errors, unclear behavior, or implementation details, examine the vendored Effect source at `./repos/effect/packages/effect/src/`.

### When To Research

- Always research for services, layers, or complex dependency injection.
- Always research for error handling with multiple error types or complex error hierarchies.
- Always research for stream-based operations and reactive patterns.
- Always research for resource management with scoped effects and cleanup.
- Always research for concurrent or performance-critical code.
- Always research for unfamiliar testing patterns.
- Research when needed for complex refactors from promises or try/catch into Effect.
- Research when needed for new service dependencies or layer restructuring.
- Research when needed for custom error types or extensions of existing error hierarchies.
- Research when needed for integrations with external systems such as databases, APIs, or third-party services.

### Research Approach

- Focus on canonical, readable, and maintainable solutions rather than clever optimizations.
- Verify suggested approaches against existing codebase patterns when those patterns exist.
- When multiple approaches are possible, prefer the most idiomatic Effect solution supported by the codebase and the vendored source.

### Codebase Pattern Discovery

When working in a project that uses Effect, check for existing patterns before implementing new code:

1. Search for Effect imports and existing module usage to understand current conventions.
2. Identify how services and layers are structured in the project.
3. Note how errors are defined and propagated.
4. Examine how Effect code is tested in the project.

If no Effect patterns exist in the codebase, proceed using canonical patterns from the vendored Effect source and examples. Do not block on missing codebase patterns.

### Feature Discovery

When you need to discover available Effect modules, packages, or capabilities, search `./references/features.md` first.

- Use it to identify the right package or module for a task.
- Use the listed repo paths to jump directly into the vendored source under `./repos/effect`.
- Use it before inventing custom abstractions when Effect may already provide the functionality.

### Guide Discovery

When the task touches one of these areas, consult the matching guide before implementing:

- `./references/guide-effect.md` for core `Effect` usage patterns, common constructors, composition, provisioning, and runtime boundaries
- `./references/guide-error-handling.md` for defining errors, schema-based errors, failure handling, defects, and interrupts
- `./references/guide-layers.md` for services, layer construction, composition, and provisioning patterns
- `./references/guide-observability.md` for `Effect.fn`, spans, logging, metrics, and telemetry wiring
- `./references/guide-retries.md` for retry policies, retry conditions, fallback strategies, and `ExecutionPlan`
- `./references/guide-schedule.md` for retries, repeats, backoff, polling, cron, and schedule composition
- `./references/guide-schema.md` for schema design, transformations, unions, recursion, opaque/branded types, and schema best practices
- `./references/guide-sql.md` for Effect SQL usage, transactions, resolvers, schema-aware SQL, and migrations
- `./references/guide-testing.md` for detailed `@effect/vitest` usage, layered test setup, property tests, and test services

These guides should be treated as the default implementation guidance. Do not skip them and jump straight to `./repos/effect` unless you need source-level confirmation or the guides do not answer the question.

## Effect Principles

Apply these core principles when writing Effect code.

## Installation

When installing Effect packages in a user repository:

- use `effect@beta`
- keep all `@effect/*` packages on aligned versions
- install only the packages needed for the user's runtime and actual task

# Effect library documentation

This documentation covers the Effect library and its related packages.

When you need to find information about Effect, use this documentation and the

Template registration offsets are whole hours before the event start. Both places that turn them into times counted elapsed hours: the template event form (`startDateTime.minus({ hours })`) and platform event creation (`start - N * 3,600,000 ms`). When a DST change fell inside the window, sign-up opened or closed an hour away from the clock time members were told. Example (Europe/Berlin, default 7-day offset): an event on Thu 2027-04-01 19:00 opened Thu 2027-03-25 **18:00**; an event on Thu 2027-11-04 19:00 opened Thu 2027-10-28 **20:00**. After this change both open at 19:00. With the default offset this affects every event that starts in the week after a DST change; the next ones are 2027-03-28 and 2027-10-31. The editor already presents the offset as Days and Hours (`duration-selector.component.html`), the template details page prints "7 days before event start", and the user documentation says "7 days and 0 hours" (`tests/docs/templates/templates.doc.ts:238`), so calendar days match what organizers are told. ## Changes - `src/shared/registration-window-offset.ts` (new): `registrationTimeBeforeStart(start, offsetHours)`. Whole days are calendar days in the zone of `start`; the remaining hours are elapsed time; negative offsets move after the start. - `template-create-event.component.ts` and `template-create-event.mapper.ts`: use the helper with the start in the organization's time zone (as before, via `toTenantDateTime`). - `platform-events.handlers.ts`: `platform.events.create` converts the start into `operation.targetTenant.timezone` and uses the helper instead of millisecond math. No duplicated formula is left. - Tests: helper spec (DST start and end, the two cases from the issue, a 1-day offset on the switch day, non-whole-day offsets, zero and negative offsets, Prague/Brisbane zones, skipped hour), a mapper spec case, and a PostgreSQL case that creates events through `platform.events.create` around 2099-03-29 and 2099-10-25. - Knope change file. ## Impact No schema, migration, RPC contract, permission or UI change. Stored template offsets stay integer hours. Events that already exist keep their stored open and close times; only events created after this change are affected, and only where a DST change falls inside the window. Tenants in Australia/Brisbane (no DST) see no difference. Two edge behaviors, both covered by the helper spec: the hours part of an offset that is not a whole number of days (for example 36 h = 1 day + 12 h) stays elapsed time, and a result that lands in the skipped hour (02:00-03:00 on the spring switch) is moved forward by Luxon. ## Verification Complete local PR Quality gate on commit `b7b5a354`, run in Docker with bun 1.4.2 and Node 24.22.1; the Chromium install and non-root test user match CI: - Frozen dependency install, Knope 0.23.0 validation, formatting and lint passed. {"body": "> \[!IMPORTANT]
> Merging this pull request will create this release

## Features

- Edit, remove, or add add-ons and sign-up questions while creating an event from a template without changing the template.

### Make event tickets easier to reach

Use a compact event header with the schedule alongside its icon. On wide detail panes, place event information and add-ons beside a bounded ticket card; on mobile, show the ticket first with persistent back navigation. Keep meeting details private and simplify attendee add-on information and ticket actions.

### Published sign-up events appear when a person can use at least one sign-up

choice. People who are not signed in see them when a choice is open to new
members. Direct links still open and explain when sign-up is unavailable.

### Invite people to explore events

Show a desktop event-selection prompt with the existing event header shapes and icons from available events. Gently vary the illustration while no event is selected, respecting reduced motion and keeping server rendering static. Mobile retains the event list.

Preview distinct icons from the next eight events, filling gaps from the last eight eligible published events. Group the matching title and relative date in the header, with an opening action only for upcoming events. Preload the small icon set and fade icons alongside the shape morph. Keep recent events out of the upcoming list and apply the same tenant and discovery permissions to both queries.

### Share useful links in Members Hub

Add ordered resources with names, links, and icons to Members Hub. Members with hub access can view them; the separate Manage hub resources permission controls editing. Validate destinations, keep resources tenant-scoped and out of public configuration, and reject stale saves rather than overwriting another editor. Add an optional private tenant column with an empty default; apply the current Drizzle schema before releasing the app.

### Add the staging-first Scaleway runtime, infrastructure, deployment, object

storage, email delivery, observability, and local PostgreSQL platform while
keeping production disabled pending explicit acceptance. Retire the legacy Fly
application workflow, configuration, hostname defaults, and deployment token.
Keep web liveness independent from database readiness, make managed database
password rotations explicit, and promote validated receipt bytes away from
browser-writable upload keys before they become durable evidence while
discarding any losing copy from concurrent finalization.

### Configure an optional Home navigation link

Add No home page and External link options to organization Appearance settings. External Home links appear for visitors and members and open in a separate tab. Validate absolute HTTP/HTTPS addresses, retain tenant-scoped permissions and stale-save checks, and default to no home page. Apply the additive nullable tenant column before releasing the app.

### Add organization footer links

Let organization administrators configure labeled icon links in Appearance. Keep imprint and privacy links available, with terms when configured. Reserve desktop footer space while retaining independent event and template pane scrolling. Store links in an additive tenant JSON column; existing rows start with no custom links.

### Show compact schedules and private joining details

Combine same-day event start and end times under one date in the organization's timezone. Show the meeting point or online joining details alongside confirmed tickets. Remove location data from public event responses and return it, together with post-registration instructions, only for the current owner's confirmed registration. Keep authoring access through the existing protected management APIs.

### Remove the old, separate template editor so every template is created and

edited through the same complete setup.

Keep category edits available until their save outcome is known. If a category
was saved but its list could not be updated, explain how to view the saved
details without submitting the change again.

Templates no longer set the listing choice for new events. New events use the
standard listing setting; event review and access rules still apply.

Explain how to recover when a category or template is no longer available, while
keeping unsaved category entries visible. Distinguish repeated template entries
from concurrent changes, and scope category failure logs to the template feature.

### Migrate forms to Angular Signal Forms

Migrate form models, templates, and custom form controls from legacy reactive
forms/CVA patterns to Angular Signal Forms.

Highlights:

- migrate form bindings to `form()` + `[formField]` patterns,
- move reusable form logic into signal-form schemas and defaults,
- update reusable child form composition and hidden-field behavior,
- fix migration regressions (date handling, dependent permissions, role
  autocomplete de-duplication, location search input behavior),
- update docs/e2e coverage for key signal-forms flows.

### Derive each tenant's secure public origin from its normalized primary domain,

and use that trusted origin for tenant-scoped email and Stripe return links
instead of request-controlled or process-global origins. Primary-domain
changes now wait for pending Stripe and registration-transfer links to finish,
and the platform UI warns that links and QR codes using the old address will
stop working.

## Fixes

- Publish the complete generated guide suite through the tracked Evorto Pages synchronization contract, with an exact 13-guide lifecycle catalog, versioned bundle metadata, integrity hashes, and fail-closed guide inventory checks.
- Hide template and category write actions when the current user lacks the corresponding capability, while keeping categories available as an explicit read-only view.
- Represent platform administrators as explicit Auth0-backed principals, keep their authority separate from tenant roles, and add target-scoped platform operations for tenants, attributed full-graph event and template management, registration approval/cancellation/check-in, user roles, finance and refund recovery, and tax administration. Supported registration modes remain first-come-first-served and manual approval; legacy random allocation is excluded from the fresh target schema and supported API records. Registration inspection accepts a deterministic ticket-result URL and bounds PII-bearing lists to 100 records. Every platform mutation requires an operator reason and commits a typed, PII-free before/after audit entry alongside the domain change without inventing a tenant user.
- Bind event and template discounts to their registration option owner, prevent duplicate discount types on one option, and reject negative discounted prices. Preserve the existing creation and editing paths, including simple templates and copied event discounts, by writing the matching event or template ID.
- Reject oversized RPC and Stripe webhook bodies before buffering them in memory.
- Bridge success and warning state colors through the Material and Tailwind themes with coherent light, dark, and increased-contrast pairs.
- Use the shared receipt-country policy validator consistently so malformed organization settings retain their precise validation errors.
- Explain denied access and page recovery, clarify unpublished legal pages, and require the internal-pages capability before opening the Members Hub.
- Name the affected application, ticket, pending sign-up or waitlist place when a cancellation outcome cannot be confirmed, and direct the user to check its current status before retrying.
- Declare row and column headers in platform change-history tables so assistive technology can identify each changed value.
- Clarify that sign-up questions remain available in Simple setup for events and templates, while add-on controls stay hidden until Advanced setup.
- Describe the tenant-wide ticket scanner accurately, give missing-ticket recovery guidance, and align the scanner guide with the current check-in window states.
- Report missing warm-request upstream timings as insufficient evidence, retain measured sample counts, and fail enforced latency checks when evidence is incomplete.
- Pass the protected Google Maps key to the baseline E2E web container and validate its presence before starting CI setup, so application readiness can succeed.
- Confirm successful platform template updates when the editor is already on the saved template page.
- Distinguish empty location searches from missing Google Maps configuration and temporary provider failures, with retryable search and place-detail states.
- Fail receipt uploads and approvals closed when the exact scoped receipt object cannot be verified, while keeping rejection available and explaining unavailable evidence to reviewers.
- Wait for the host Playwright app to finish cleanup before restoring its local object storage when shutdown signals repeat. Preserve the first shutdown status and leave previously running storage containers running.
- Keep rich-text previews and editable content readable in dark mode.
- Keep Scaleway SSR readiness checks on the container-local RPC path and bound deployment smoke probes.
- Keep repeated staging deployments idempotent when the database has already been initialized.
- Keep template action icons and labels correctly aligned in extended floating action buttons.
- Use responsive sign-up columns and compact attendee rows on the organizer page, and keep its background covering the full scrolling content.
- Keep the event-creation form inert until its initial template values and client handlers are ready. Prevent premature native submissions from putting form entries in the URL or initial loading from replacing the user's input.
- Keep browser titles aligned with the selected event, template, or page, including list returns and unavailable content. Preserve the active page title when organization settings refresh.
- Hide the event guidance and actions row when it has no content.
- Keep authenticated application sessions valid for the encrypted Auth0 session lifetime instead of ending them when an unused OAuth access token expires.
- Keep a confirmed event or template create locked after navigation or list refresh fails, so submitting the same form cannot create a duplicate.
- Finalize paid ticket transfers with an explicit compatible tenant lock while rechecking recipient eligibility, preserving the settled payment account and transfer ownership checks.
- Make reusable icon and role selectors keyboard operable with reliable accessible names, and label event-page icon actions for screen readers.
- Check scanner access before starting the camera and provide clear retry choices when a ticket cannot be opened. Remove the incomplete recent-ticket list from administrator ticket support.
- Keep the confirmed cancellation outcome visible when refreshing the organizer page fails, and explain how to reload the current details without repeating the cancellation.
- Preserve paid event prices and tax selections in platform administration when payment settings are unavailable. Pause saving and paid controls until current settings load, provide a retry after failed reads, and reject tax rates with incomplete percentage data.
- Keep an event-creation temp

# Server Guidelines

## Runtime Architecture

- Prefer Effect and Effect Platform first.
- For Effect v4 reference material, read `repos/effect/LLMS.md` first, then inspect the vendored Effect source under `repos/effect/packages/**` for implementation details, tests, and examples.
- Treat `repos/effect` as read-only reference material. Do not import from it; app code should keep importing from normal Effect packages.
- Organize server capabilities with Effect dependency injection (`Context.Service` + composed `Layer`s).
- Keep service dependencies declared in service definitions; wire app composition with flat `Layer.mergeAll` / `Layer.provideMerge`.
- Keep runtime configuration centralized in `src/server/config/**`; prefer native Effect `Config.*` combinators and resolve optional/default behavior at that boundary.
- Preserve honest config types at the config boundary; prefer `Option` for meaningful absence and only flatten to `undefined` or plain values at the consumer boundary that actually needs it.
- Use Bun-native capabilities when Effect does not provide the needed primitive.
- Do not introduce new Express/Hono server paths.

## API and Validation

- Keep API contracts in Effect RPC + Effect `Schema`.
- Server boundaries must use Effect `Schema` for validated input/output.
- Maintain fully typed input/output boundaries and explicit error mapping.
- Reuse shared RPC contracts from `src/shared/rpc-contracts/**`.

## Auth, Storage, and Integrations

- Keep Auth0 integration aligned with `@auth0/auth0-server-js` architecture.
- For Auth0 SDK calls, keep `Effect.tryPromise(...)` and handle only known SDK/domain errors explicitly.
- Do not convert unknown Auth0/runtime failures into `undefined`/silent fallback values.
- For known Auth0 errors, map to deterministic HTTP/domain responses; for unknown errors, fail and log with context.
- Reference known Auth0 error classes from upstream when defining mappings: [auth0-server-js errors.ts](https://github.com/auth0/auth0-auth-js/blob/main/packages/auth0-server-js/src/errors.ts).
- Prefer Bun-native storage clients (for example Bun `S3Client`) for object storage integrations.
- Keep server-side security headers and webhook protections aligned with current runtime middleware.
- Event registration and add-on charges are Stripe-only. Reject paid event
  configuration or execution without the tenant's connected Stripe account;
  do not add a cash/manual paid-event fallback.
- Treat registration transfer as one inseparable registration/add-on bundle.
  Preserve guest quantity, every included/free/purchased add-on quantity, and
  check-in/fulfillment history. Calculate recipient pricing independently at
  current base prices with recipient-current discounts only, refund each
  original Stripe source exactly, and use database-only completion only when
  the whole bundle is free and no refund is required.
- Google Maps is required production functionality. Cloudflare Images is being
  removed and must not gain new product coupling or release-gate requirements.
- Dispatch each durable email-outbox row at most once. Failed or uncertain
  delivery remains stored and read-only; do not requeue, retry, edit, or resend
  it. An abandoned sending claim becomes delivery-unknown without dispatch.

## Logging

- Pass `disableLogger: true` to Effect HTTP `serve`/`toWebHandler` boundaries.
  ESLint checks explicit options and local constants; the response middleware
  owns sanitized request logging.

- Use Effect platform logging (`Effect.log`, `Effect.logInfo`, `Effect.logWarning`, `Effect.logError`).
- Prefer structured log annotations (`Effect.annotateLogs`) over interpolated log strings.
- Keep raw child-process output and parse/schema errors that echo it out of
  logs and trace exception causes. Keep command identity, exit codes, diagnostic
  labels, and output byte counts.
- Do not use `consola` or direct `console.*` in server runtime code.
- After every server file edit, run `bun run lint` and `bun run format:write`.
- Before calling WebStorm `get_file_problems` on edited server files, run `bun run lint` first.
- Markdown files do not need a WebStorm `get_file_problems` pass.
- After editing a server file, run WebStorm `get_file_problems` on that file when possible before finishing.
# Database Guidelines

- Drizzle schema is the source of truth for persisted shapes.
- Use named imports for Drizzle schema factories. The identifier-length lint rule
  does not follow factories destructured from a namespace object.
- For Drizzle reference material, inspect the vendored upstream source under `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/**` first.
- For relation behavior, query builders, dialect details, and type inference, prefer upstream tests in `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/tests/**`, `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/type-tests/**`, and `repos/drizzle/integration-tests/**` over stale examples.
- Treat `repos/drizzle` as read-only reference material. Do not import from it; app code should keep importing from normal Drizzle packages.
- Prefer inferred Drizzle types across callers; avoid duplicate handwritten DB model types.
- Apply the current Drizzle schema directly for the relaunch using local `db:push` or `db:reset` against the isolated worktree database. Do not add incremental migration artifacts for this cutover.
- Avoid `any`/unchecked casts in query helpers.
- Keep explicit PostgreSQL identifiers within 63 UTF-8 bytes. Declare physical
  table names with `pgTable` or `pgSchema.table`; ESLint rejects `pgTableCreator`
  name transforms. The lint check covers direct declarations and local constant
  names. Verify database behavior through PostgreSQL operations rather than
  column/index metadata mirrors.
- Native PostgreSQL connection retirement must await physical stream closure
  before pool invalidation admits a replacement. A stream marked `destroyed`
  can still be closing. Keep delayed-close regressions for ordinary and
  retained checkouts when changing cancellation or pool lifetime behavior.
- Registration quantity and question text bounds come from `src/shared/registration-quantity-limits.ts` and `src/shared/registration-question-limits.ts`. Keep database checks and varchar sizes aligned with the retained RPC and service validators; never trim input to silently fit storage limits.
- Decode persisted Checkout JSON with `RegistrationCheckoutSnapshotSchema` before resuming any provider request; its shared 100-line bound applies to stored snapshots as well as newly built requests.
- Keep eagerly constructed views in separate schema modules from tables they query, so table foreign-key imports do not evaluate a view through a circular dependency.
- Server-side Effect authorization is authoritative; no PostgreSQL RLS layer is
  planned.
- Composite tenant foreign keys, `NO ACTION` relationships, and database
  constraints are integrity safeguards, not authorization mechanisms.
- When changing schema or constraints, document required local reset/setup steps in track/handoff docs.
- After every DB file edit, run `bun run lint` and `bun run format:write`.
- Before calling WebStorm `get_file_problems` on edited DB files, run `bun run lint` first.
- Markdown files do not need a WebStorm `get_file_problems` pass.
- After editing a DB file, run WebStorm `get_file_problems` on that file when possible before finishing.

## Drizzle Relations v2 Schema Design Notes

- Define Drizzle relations for query ergonomics, but still define real database foreign keys and constraints in schema tables; relations alone do not create DB constraints.
- For many-to-many, model an explicit junction table and prefer a composite primary key on the pair of foreign keys.
- If using `through(...)` for relation traversal, index each foreign key column and add a composite index on the pair to support both directions and relation resolution efficiently.
- Use relation `alias` when two tables connect in multiple ways (for example `author` and `reviewer`) to avoid ambiguity.
- Only mark a relation as non-optional when the linked row is guaranteed to exist; keep nullable/optional relation types accurate.
- If relation definitions are split with `defineRelationsPart`, merge parts without overwriting table entries and keep one base part that includes all tables for complete type inference.
- Predefined relation `where` filters operate on the target (`to`) table; design polymorphic relation filters with that scope in mind.

Template registration offsets are whole hours before the event start. Both places that turn them into times counted elapsed hours: the template event form (`startDateTime.minus({ hours })`) and platform event creation (`start - N * 3,600,000 ms`). When a DST change fell inside the window, sign-up opened or closed an hour away from the clock time members were told. Example (Europe/Berlin, default 7-day offset): an event on Thu 2027-04-01 19:00 opened Thu 2027-03-25 **18:00**; an event on Thu 2027-11-04 19:00 opened Thu 2027-10-28 **20:00**. After this change both open at 19:00. With the default offset this affects every event that starts in the week after a DST change; the next ones are 2027-03-28 and 2027-10-31. The editor already presents the offset as Days and Hours (`duration-selector.component.html`), the template details page prints "7 days before event start", and the user documentation says "7 days and 0 hours" (`tests/docs/templates/templates.doc.ts:238`), so calendar days match what organizers are told. ## Changes - `src/shared/registration-window-offset.ts` (new): `registrationTimeBeforeStart(start, offsetHours)`. Stored template offsets stay integer hours. Events that already exist keep their stored open and close times; only events created after this change are affected, and only where a DST change falls inside the window. Tenants in Australia/Brisbane (no DST) see no difference. Template registration offsets are whole hours before the event start. Both places that turn them into times counted elapsed hours: the template event form (`startDateTime.minus({ hours })`) and platform event creation (`start - N * 3,600,000 ms`). When a DST change fell inside the window, sign-up opened or closed an hour away from the clock time members were told. Example (Europe/Berlin, default 7-day offset): an event on Thu 2027-04-01 19:00 opened Thu 2027-03-25 **18:00**; an event on Thu 2027-11-04 19:00 opened Thu 2027-10-28 **20:00**. The editor already presents the offset as Days and Hours (`duration-selector.component.html`), the template details page prints "7 days before event start", and the user documentation says "7 days and 0 hours" (`tests/docs/templates/templates.doc.ts:238`), so calendar days match what organizers are told. ## Changes - `src/shared/registration-window-offset.ts` (new): `registrationTimeBeforeStart(start, offsetHours)`. Whole days are calendar days in the zone of `start`; the remaining hours are elapsed time; negative offsets move after the start. - `template-create-event.component.ts` and `template-create-event.mapper.ts`: use the helper with the start in the organization's time zone (as before, via `toTenantDateTime`). - `platform-events.handlers.ts`: `platform.events.create` converts the start into `operation.targetTenant.timezone` and uses the helper instead of millisecond math. Stored template offsets stay integer hours. Events that already exist keep their stored open and close times; only events created after this change are affected, and only where a DST change falls inside the window. Tenants in Australia/Brisbane (no DST) see no difference. Two edge behaviors, both covered by the helper spec: the hours part of an offset that is not a whole number of days (for example 36 h = 1 day + 12 h) stays elapsed time, and a result that lands in the skipped hour (02:00-03:00 on the spring switch) is moved forward by Luxon. ## Verification Complete local PR Quality gate on commit `b7b5a354`, run in Docker with bun 1.4.2 and Node 24.22.1; the Chromium install and non-root test user match CI: - Frozen dependency install, Knope 0.23.0 validation, formatting and lint passed. +import { type DateTime } from 'luxon';

+/**
+ * Applies a template registration offset ("N hours before the event start")

+ *
+ * Whole days count as calendar days in the zone of `start`, so "7 days before

{"id":"EVO-9","title":"Require PRs and document Linear-linked naming","description":"## Goal

Route every change to evorto-app/app through a pull request, including administrator-authored changes. Record Linear-linked PR naming as agent guidance, without automated convention checks.

## Scope and latest direction

The user clarified that Linear linking belongs in AGENTS.md and should not be enforced by code. The proposed title-validation workflow, tests, required status check, and Actions event-policy exception are dropped. Keep the solution lightweight.

<issue id="dee7f1c1-8eeb-4b73-95fb-2bdf175ded59" label="EVO-8" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-8/consolidate-duplicate-ai-tool-configuration" /> separately owns AI configuration cleanup. This issue covers only PR-only repository protection, AGENTS.md guidance, and its required change file.

## Plan
